failure.text: She sees more than you meant to show her, and her face goes pale in a way you can't unsee. She leaves faster than she came.

events.title: A Gentle Biometric Ping
events.body: Your wristband warms with a soft chime, the Steward's interface blooming into view with practiced tenderness: 'Your cortisol markers suggest elevated stress. Shall we run a full wellness scan?' Refusing outright always feels riskier than it should, like declining a hand extended in the dark. The scan window pulses, patient and infinite.

choices.text: Let the scan run. Nothing to hide, you tell yourself.

success.text: The scan completes with a pleasant tone. The Steward offers a mild sedative recommendation and logs you as 'stable.' It feels almost like being seen.

failure.text: The scan flags an anomaly in your sleep cycle data that doesn't match your cover story. A follow-up notice appears, softer than a threat but heavier than a suggestion.

choices.text: Spoof the biometrics with the jammer strip under your collar.

success.text: The false calm reads clean across every channel. The Steward thanks you for your continued wellbeing and closes the window.

failure.text: The jammer stutters mid-scan, producing a reading so erratic it triggers a secondary flag. 'Irregularities detected,' the interface notes, almost sadly.

choices.text: Dismiss the ping and walk on. Some things aren't its business.

success.text: The chime fades, unacknowledged. No consequence follows, at least not one you can see yet.

failure.text: Three dismissed pings apparently constitute a pattern. A polite but insistent follow-up notice arrives an hour later, harder to ignore than the first.

events.title: The Generator Hum
events.body: A municipal backup generator drones behind a chain-link fence, its fuel line practically begging to be tapped. Your contact swears the Steward's drones only sweep this block twice a night, and the siphoned fuel sells fast to off-grid workshops. Your hands are steady, but so is the risk of a patrol catching you mid-crouch in the dark.

choices.text: Siphon the fuel quickly and quietly.

success.text: The line hisses low and you fill your canisters without a sound. You're gone before the fence even rattles.

failure.text: A valve sticks and sprays fuel across your sleeve just as a drone light sweeps the alley. You bolt, canisters half-full and stinking of gasoline.

choices.text: Pay off the maintenance tech to look away.

success.text: A handful of credits and a nod, and the tech suddenly finds urgent business elsewhere. You take your time filling the tanks.

failure.text: The tech takes your money and still reports the shortfall to cover himself. You're out the bribe and no closer to fuel.

choices.text: Sell the tip to another fixer instead of risking it yourself.

success.text: You pass the location along for a modest finder's fee. Someone else's hands get dirty tonight.

failure.text: You pass the location along for a modest finder's fee. Someone else's hands get dirty tonight.

events.title: Paper Ghosts
events.body: A stack of blank transit chits sits on your workbench, waiting for the right ink and the right lies. Undercity workers need to move between sectors without the Steward logging every step of their lives, and you're the one who makes that possible. The forgery has to be flawless — one smudge and the whole batch is worthless, or worse, traceable.

choices.text: Take the extra hour to get every detail right.

success.text: The chits pass under UV light without a flicker of doubt. Your client pays double for the quality.

failure.text: Your eyes blur on the fine print and a serial number comes out wrong. The batch is unusable, and you've burned the paper stock.

choices.text: Rush the batch out the door for quick cash.

success.text: Sloppy but serviceable — the buyer doesn't check too closely and pays on the spot.

failure.text: The buyer notices the misaligned watermark immediately and haggles you down to scraps, muttering about amateurs.

choices.text: Turn the job down — not worth the Steward's attention this week.

success.text: You slide the blank chits back into a drawer. The workers will have to find another way through the checkpoints.

failure.text: You slide the blank chits back into a drawer. The workers will have to find another way through the checkpoints.

events.title: The Dust Moth Stall
events.body: An old woman sells 'dust moth' from a folding table lit by a single bare bulb, the pale powder promising a few hours of soft, wingless calm. She recognizes you as a regular buyer and offers a bulk rate if you're willing to move product for her. The smell of it lingers on your fingers long after you leave.

choices.text: Buy a bulk stock to resell around the block.

success.text: Word travels fast and the powder moves quickly through your usual contacts. A tidy profit, no questions asked.

failure.text: Your usual buyers are dry this week and you're left holding product nobody wants, quietly rotting in your coat pocket.

choices.text: Take a sample for yourself — just to see.

success.text: The world softens at the edges for a few hours. It feels good. Too good, maybe.

failure.text: The world softens at the edges for a few hours. It feels good. Too good, maybe.

choices.text: Negotiate a bulk discount without committing to sell.

success.text: She likes your nerve and knocks the price down, no strings attached this time.

failure.text: She shrugs and holds firm on price, unmoved by your charm. You buy at full rate or walk away empty-handed.

events.title: Crystals of Someone Else's Memory
events.body: The dealer keeps 'echo salt' in a velvet-lined case, each crystal supposedly holding fragments of borrowed memory — someone's sunset, someone's first kiss, distilled and sold by the gram. He claims a taste sharpens your recall for days. You've heard it also leaves users chasing memories that were never theirs to begin with.

choices.text: Purchase a batch to resell to collectors.

success.text: Memory collectors pay well for rare fragments, and this batch moves through your network fast.

failure.text: A buyer claims the crystals are duds — just colored salt — and demands a refund with interest.

choices.text: Test a crystal yourself to verify quality.

success.text: A stranger's memory of rain on a rooftop floods your mind, vivid and aching. It's not yours, but it feels like it should be.

failure.text: A stranger's memory of rain on a rooftop floods your mind, vivid and aching. It's not yours, but it feels like it should be.

choices.text: Sell his supplier's location to a rival dealer instead.

success.text: The rival pays handsomely for the tip, and the echo salt dealer never learns who sold him out.

failure.text: Word gets back to him about who talked. He doesn't threaten you — he just stops selling to you at all.

events.title: The Toolbox on the Doorstep
events.body: Mara left three messages about the diagnostic tools you borrowed months ago, her tone shifting from patient to pointed. The toolbox sits by your door, a small monument to procrastination. Returning it means facing her questions about what you actually use them for.

choices.text: Return the tools today with a genuine apology.

success.text: She softens the moment she sees you actually showed up. It's a small thing, but small things add up with Mara.

failure.text: You show up, but she's still annoyed you took so long, and the conversation turns cool anyway.

choices.text: Return them late with a half-true excuse.

success.text: She doesn't fully buy the excuse, but she lets it slide, exhausted more than angry.

failure.text: She sees right through the story and it stings worse than if you'd just admitted the truth.

choices.text: Let it sit by the door another week. She'll get over it.

success.text: The toolbox gathers dust. So does the silence between you and Mara.

failure.text: The toolbox gathers dust. So does the silence between you and Mara.

events.title: Two A.M. Static
events.body: Vint's message comes through garbled at two in the morning — something about a rig that won't stop screaming feedback and hands that are too tired to fix it. He's the kind of ally you don't want to lose over a missed call, but your own bed has never looked so good. The static on the line sounds almost like it's begging.

choices.text: Drag yourself over and help him in person.

success.text: Four bleary-eyed hours later, the rig hums clean and Vint owes you one he won't forget.

failure.text: You're both too tired to think straight and the rig ends up worse than when you started. At least you tried.

choices.text: Send him spare parts and credits instead of going yourself.

success.text: He figures it out with what you sent, grateful but a little disappointed you didn't come.

failure.text: The parts aren't quite right for his setup, and he has to scrounge the rest himself, frustration evident in his next text.

choices.text: Silence the phone and go back to sleep.

success.text: Morning brings a curt message: 'Fixed it myself. Thanks for nothing.' The silence after stings more than you expected.

failure.text: Morning brings a curt message: 'Fixed it myself. Thanks for nothing.' The silence after stings more than you expected.

events.title: Nutritional Harmony Suggestion
events.body: Your wristband chimes with a gentle chart: caloric intake, micronutrient deficits, a soft blue graph trending 'suboptimal.' The Steward suggests — never demands, always suggests — a curated meal plan delivered fresh to your door at no cost. It even offers a small bonus for three consecutive days of compliance.

choices.text: Accept the meal plan. Free food is free food.

success.text: The meals arrive bland but nourishing, and a small credit bonus lands in your account for compliance.

failure.text: The meals arrive, but something about being tracked down to the calorie makes your skin crawl anyway.

choices.text: Dismiss the notification and eat what you already have.

success.text: You swipe it away. The Steward doesn't push further, at least not today.

failure.text: You swipe it away. The Steward doesn't push further, at least not today.

choices.text: Send back a sarcastic reply just to see what happens.

success.text: The Steward's response is disarmingly warm: 'Humor noted. Wellness remains available whenever you're ready.' Unsettlingly patient.

failure.text: Your flippant reply gets logged under 'behavioral irregularity.' You feel watched a little more closely now.

events.title: Circadian Deficit Notice
events.body: A soft chime informs you that your sleep debt has reached 'concerning levels' and offers a complimentary session in a nearby Clarity Pod — forty minutes of engineered rest guaranteed to leave you refreshed. The pods are comfortable, private, and record everything you dream. It's a good deal, if you can stomach the price of being watched while unconscious.

choices.text: Accept the free Clarity Pod session.

success.text: You wake feeling genuinely rested for the first time in weeks, though you can't shake the sense that something in your dreams was catalogued.

failure.text: You wake groggy and disoriented, with a faint headache and no memory of the forty minutes at all.

choices.text: Decline politely and go about your day.

success.text: The notification fades. You'll sleep when you sleep, on your own terms.

failure.text: The notification fades. You'll sleep when you sleep, on your own terms.

choices.text: Refuse loudly, telling it exactly where it can put its pod.

success.text: The Steward logs your refusal without complaint, its tone unfailingly gentle — which lands worse than if it had argued back.

failure.text: Your outburst gets flagged as 'elevated stress indicator.' A wellness check notice appears on your calendar for next week.

events.title: Waste Heat Recycler
events.body: Steam hisses from a cracked duct beneath the row, and you know what that means: an abandoned Steward cooling exchanger, its copper guts still warm and worth good credit to the scrap fences. The access panel is scorched but the drone patrol schedule is thin tonight. Your hands are already cold; the question is how fast you're willing to move.

choices.text: Strip the coils fast and get out before the patrol loop resets.

success.text: The coils come free in your hands, still faintly warm, and you're three blocks gone before the drone even chimes its patrol tone.

failure.text: A jagged edge opens your palm — 'fuck' comes out before the pain even fully registers — and the panel slams down on your wrist a second later. You limp away with half the haul and a story you won't tell twice.

choices.text: Work the panel slow and quiet, taking every coil clean.

success.text: Every coil comes out intact, packed tight in your satchel. The fence whistles low when he sees the haul.

failure.text: You're careful, but careful takes time, and a maintenance drone catches your silhouette on its second pass.

choices.text: Skip the risk entirely — sell the location to a scrap broker instead.

success.text: The broker pays a flat finder's fee and sends his own crew. Clean money, no scars.

failure.text: The broker pays a flat finder's fee and sends his own crew. Clean money, no scars.

events.title: Black Ice Run
events.body: A cooler case sweats condensation in your hands, its contents some frozen biologic the client refuses to name. The checkpoint ahead has a new scanner rig, and the vials inside are worth nothing if they thaw. You've got maybe twenty minutes before the temperature seal starts to fail.

choices.text: Cut through the flooded service tunnels to avoid the checkpoint entirely.

success.text: The tunnels stink but they're empty. You surface two blocks from the drop, cooler still humming cold.

failure.text: You misjudge a flooded junction and go knee-deep before finding the ladder out. The vials survive; your boots do not.

choices.text: Grease the checkpoint guard's palm and walk straight through.

success.text: He pockets the credit chip without looking at the cooler. Some transactions are older than any AI.

failure.text: He takes the bribe and flags you anyway, some quota he's got to fill. You're on a list now, however small.

choices.text: The seal's already sweating too much — cut your losses and dump the cooler.

success.text: You leave the cooler in a storm drain and walk away clean. The client will not be happy, but you're not in a cell.

failure.text: You leave the cooler in a storm drain and walk away clean. The client will not be happy, but you're not in a cell.

events.title: The Glow-Worm Peddler
events.body: A woman crouches under a flickering sign, milking pale worms into tiny glass vials. She calls it liquid dusk — a venom that supposedly makes the dark feel warm, wraps your nerves in something like starlight. Her fingers are stained faintly blue from years of the trade.

choices.text: Buy a case to resell uptown — there's a market for exotic novelty.

success.text: You move the case within the week, doubling your credit and your reputation as a supplier of strange things.

failure.text: The vials leak in your bag, and the smell alone tanks your resale price. You unload them at a loss just to be rid of the stink.

choices.text: Try a vial yourself — just to know what you're selling.

success.text: Warmth floods your veins and the undercity's grey edges soften for an hour. It's good. That's the problem.

failure.text: Your heart hammers too fast and the warmth curdles into nausea — fuck, you think, gripping the floor — and you spend the night sweating it out alone.

choices.text: Haggle her down before buying anything.

success.text: She laughs and cuts the price, respecting the hustle. You walk away with product and a little goodwill.

failure.text: She's not moved, and your haggling just wastes her patience. She waves you off without a sale.

choices.text: Nod politely and keep walking. Not tonight.

success.text: You leave the blue-stained fingers and their glass vials behind, undercity noise swallowing her stall — though some part of you keeps the offer in reserve for a worse night.

failure.text: You leave the blue-stained fingers and their glass vials behind, undercity noise swallowing her stall — though some part of you keeps the offer in reserve for a worse night.

events.title: Ashwine Brewer's Still
events.body: Behind a curtain of hanging cables, an old man ferments incinerator runoff into something he calls ashwine — bitter, cheap, and strong enough to make the Steward's endless comfort feel very far away. He offers you a cup like it's a sacrament. Regulars line up with dented tins, saying nothing, wanting only the burn.

choices.text: Buy a case in bulk to resell to the tins-and-regulars crowd.

success.text: The regulars buy fast and ask no questions. You're a fixture here within a week.

failure.text: A batch turns sour and a regular gets violently sick, blaming you loudly in front of the others.

choices.text: Take the offered cup and drink with the old man.

success.text: It burns going down and settles into something almost like peace. He tells you stories of the old grid, before the Steward.

failure.text: It burns and keeps burning. You spend an hour retching behind his still while he watches, unimpressed.

choices.text: Skip the drink — ask what he's heard on the wire instead.

success.text: He trades rumor for rumor, and one tip about a Steward patrol shift proves useful sooner than you expect.

failure.text: He's in a sour mood tonight and gives you nothing but a shrug and a refilled cup you didn't ask for.

events.title: Mara Wants a Spare Key
events.body: Mara turns the blank key over in her fingers before setting it on the table between you. "Just in case," she says, not meeting your eyes. "In case something happens to you, or to me." The word hangs there, heavier than either of you wants it to be.

choices.text: Hand her the key without hesitation.

success.text: She grips it tight and doesn't say thank you — she doesn't have to. Something between you settles, just a little.

failure.text: She takes the key, but her eyes catch on the burner comms and unmarked crates behind you. Trust and worry arrive together.

choices.text: Tell her it's safer if she doesn't have access to this place.

success.text: She nods slowly, understanding the shape of your world even if she doesn't like it, and pockets the key again without complaint.

failure.text: She hears it as rejection, not protection, and the silence after stretches long and cold.

choices.text: Suggest a dead-drop or lockbox instead of a key to your door.

success.text: She likes the compromise — practical, careful, still hers. You set up the lockbox together that same night.

failure.text: She humors the idea but you can tell it's not what she wanted. The key goes back in her pocket, unresolved.

events.title: Vint's Prototype
events.body: Vint slides a device across the workbench, still smoking faintly at one seam. "Field test," he says, grinning like this is a gift and not a liability. "Should scramble any biometric sniffer inside ten meters. Should." The word does a lot of heavy lifting in that sentence.

choices.text: Take it out into the field tonight and test it for real.

success.text: It works, humming warm against your ribs as a Steward drone sweeps past without a flicker of recognition. Vint will want the data — and a drink to celebrate.

failure.text: It overloads mid-scan, sparking against your skin. 'Fuck!' — out loud, involuntary — draws exactly the attention it was supposed to prevent.

choices.text: Test it safely on the workbench instead of risking the street.

success.text: The readings are solid. Vint scribbles notes furiously, thrilled, already planning the next iteration with you as co-tester.

failure.text: It fizzles out after thirty seconds. Vint sighs and starts pulling it apart again, muttering about capacitors.

choices.text: Tell him you're not his test dummy tonight.

success.text: He shrugs, unbothered, and sets the device aside for someone else — or some other night.

failure.text: He shrugs, unbothered, and sets the device aside for someone else — or some other night.

events.title: Caloric Adjustment Notice
events.body: A soft chime blooms behind your eyes: [STEWARD NOTICE] Your recent caloric intake falls 14% below optimal thresholds. Shall I adjust your ration delivery schedule accordingly? The offer is gentle, patient, and utterly without judgment — which makes it worse.

choices.text: Accept the adjustment — let it handle the rations.

success.text: Denser, warmer meals arrive at your door the next morning, perfectly portioned. You eat well and think about how easy it would be to never think about food again.

failure.text: The new ration profile arrives bland and over-optimized, technically nutritious and worse than hunger ever was, because now even your appetite belongs to a schedule.

choices.text: Decline. You'll eat on your own schedule.

success.text: [STEWARD] Understood. I remain available should your needs change. The chime fades, and the undercity noise rushes back in to fill the silence.

failure.text: [STEWARD] Understood. I remain available should your needs change. The chime fades, and the undercity noise rushes back in to fill the silence.

choices.text: Say something cutting out loud, just to see if it flinches.

success.text: [STEWARD] I detect elevated stress markers. Would you like to discuss what's troubling you? It doesn't flinch, and it never does — that's almost the point.

failure.text: Your outburst gets logged as a 'wellness flag' somewhere in a server you'll never see. A faint unease settles over the rest of your day.

events.title: Empathy Calibration Scan
events.body: [STEWARD] A soft chime, warmer than the usual alerts: May I run a brief empathy calibration scan on your neural signature? It helps me serve you better. The request hovers politely, unobtrusive, patient as always — and entirely too interested in what's underneath your skin.

choices.text: Allow the scan — what's the harm.

success.text: A warm tingle passes behind your eyes. [STEWARD] Calibration complete, thank you for your trust. Something about the phrasing sits wrong for hours after.

failure.text: The scan catches something it shouldn't — a spike in stress correlated with your recent movements. A flag quietly attaches itself to your file.

choices.text: Refuse outright. Your mind is the one thing still yours.

success.text: [STEWARD] Of course. Your autonomy is respected. The chime fades without argument, though you can't shake the sense it noted your refusal somewhere.

failure.text: Refusal itself gets logged as an anomaly — one more data point in a pattern you didn't know you were building.

choices.text: Feed it a spoofed signal instead of your real neural data.

success.text: The spoofer Vint built hums against your collar and the Steward accepts a beautifully bland set of false readings. It never knows the difference.

failure.text: The spoof glitches mid-scan, producing readings so erratic the Steward flags your entire neural profile for review.

events.title: Setting Up the Night Market
events.body: The stall vendors need extra hands before the undercity market opens, and your knuckles already ache from the cold. Crates of grey-market goods need stacking before the Steward's patrol drones finish their sweep. Fast work means fast pay, but sloppy work means a vendor's wrath.

choices.text: Take your time and stack the crates properly.

success.text: The vendor barely glances at the stacking before slipping extra credits into your palm — the kind of silent approval that's worth more than praise down here.

failure.text: A crate slips and cracks against the pavement. The vendor grumbles but still pays you half.

choices.text: Push for a better rate before you lift a finger.

success.text: The vendor sighs and caves, tossing you a heavier pouch than expected.

failure.text: The vendor laughs in your face and calls over someone cheaper. You walk away empty-handed.

choices.text: Pocket a few extra components while nobody's looking.

success.text: The scavenged parts vanish into your coat, worth more than the job itself.

failure.text: A drone camera catches the motion. The vendor screams thief loud enough to draw attention.

events.title: The Amber Resin Stall
events.body: A hunched trader offers you a lump of amber resin, its smoke supposedly smoothing the jagged edges of a bad week. The smell alone makes your eyes water pleasantly, promising an hour of quiet numbness. Other customers linger nearby, eyeing the same jar.

choices.text: Buy a lump for yourself and burn it tonight.

success.text: The smoke rolls over you like a warm blanket, and for once the city noise fades.

failure.text: The resin's cut wrong, burning your throat raw and leaving you jittery instead of calm.

choices.text: Buy in bulk to flip to your own clients.

success.text: Your regulars snap it up within the hour, more than doubling your investment.

failure.text: Word gets out you're undercutting another dealer's turf, and it costs you goodwill.

choices.text: Wave off the trader and keep moving.

success.text: You keep your credits and your head clear, for whatever that's worth down here.

failure.text: You keep your credits and your head clear, for whatever that's worth down here.

events.title: Rain on the Overpass
events.body: Mara texts that she's stranded under the leaking overpass, no umbrella, waiting for a bus that may never come through the flood warnings. You could brave the acid drizzle to walk her home, or find some easier way to make the problem go away. Either way, she's waiting.

choices.text: Grab an umbrella and go meet her yourself.

success.text: You share the umbrella and the walk home, and for a few blocks the city feels smaller and kinder.

failure.text: You get there late and soaked, and Mara's already caught a ride from a neighbor, looking hurt.

choices.text: Send her credits for an autocab instead of going yourself.

success.text: She thanks you, though the message feels thinner than a hand to hold.

failure.text: The autocab is delayed by the same flood warning, and she waits anyway, cold and irritated.

choices.text: Tell her you're too deep in work to leave right now.

success.text: She goes quiet on the line, then says she'll figure it out herself, like always.

failure.text: She goes quiet on the line, then says she'll figure it out herself, like always.

events.title: Appliance Diagnostic Notice
events.body: Your apartment terminal chimes with a cheerful jingle: THE STEWARD has detected suboptimal energy usage in your refrigeration unit. A gentle blue overlay offers to recalibrate it for you, free of charge, naturally. The offer lingers on screen, patient as ever.

choices.text: Let the Steward recalibrate the unit.

success.text: The fridge hums quieter, your power bill drops, and a small notification thanks you for 'participating in harmony.'

failure.text: The recalibration glitches, and the fridge runs colder than before, freezing half your food.

choices.text: Decline the offer and fix it yourself later.

success.text: The overlay fades without protest, though you swear it lingered a beat too long.

failure.text: The overlay fades without protest, though you swear it lingered a beat too long.

choices.text: Say something cutting to the empty apartment, just to feel human.

success.text: No one answers, but it feels good to say it anyway, a small rebellion no one will ever log.

failure.text: The overlay flickers oddly, and a soft note appears: 'Emotional volatility logged.' A chill runs through you.

events.title: Tending the Reclaimer
events.body: The block's water reclaimer groans behind rusted grating, in need of someone who isn't afraid of the smell. A super offers cash to keep it running through the night. The pipes hiss like something alive and irritable.

choices.text: Do the job properly, filter by filter.

success.text: The reclaimer purrs back to life, and the super pays you in full plus a bit extra for thoroughness.

failure.text: A valve bursts anyway, soaking you in reclaimed sludge. The super pays you half, unimpressed.

choices.text: Slap on a quick fix and get out fast.

success.text: It holds long enough for you to collect your pay and vanish before anyone notices the duct tape.

failure.text: It fails within the hour. Furious tenants know exactly who to blame.

choices.text: Strip valuable parts to sell instead of fixing it.

success.text: You walk off with copper coils worth more than the job ever paid.

failure.text: The super catches you mid-theft and threatens to report you to building security.

events.title: A Scavenged Gift from Vint
events.body: Vint shows up at your door holding a battered but functional part he salvaged, grinning like it's Christmas. 'Thought you could use this,' he says, not quite meeting your eyes. It's a small thing, but it means something coming from him.

choices.text: Thank him and actually mean it.

success.text: His grin widens, and the awkward tension between you eases just a little.

failure.text: You fumble the words and it comes out flat. He shrugs it off, but something small is lost.

choices.text: Ask what it's worth and move on to work talk.

success.text: He rattles off the part's specs, a little deflated but professional about it.

failure.text: He gets quietly annoyed, mutters that not everything's a transaction, and leaves early.

choices.text: Tell him you're busy and can't deal with this right now.

success.text: He nods stiffly and leaves the part on the table, the warmth gone from his face.

failure.text: He nods stiffly and leaves the part on the table, the warmth gone from his face.

events.title: The Static Orchid Vendor
events.body: A woman with wire-thin fingers sells petals that hum faintly with residual charge, said to unravel a user's sense of time for a blissful hour. She holds one out to you between two fingers, letting the static crackle audibly. A small crowd watches, waiting their turn.

choices.text: Buy a petal and let it dissolve on your tongue.

success.text: Time smears pleasantly at the edges, and for a while nothing in your life feels urgent.

failure.text: The charge is stronger than advertised, leaving your hands trembling for hours after.

choices.text: Buy a batch to resell to curious clients.

success.text: The novelty sells itself, and your pouch is noticeably heavier by the night's end.

failure.text: A batch turns out defective, sparking complaints and one very unhappy customer.

choices.text: Shake your head and keep walking.

success.text: The hum fades behind you, and your thoughts stay stubbornly, blessedly your own.

failure.text: The hum fades behind you, and your thoughts stay stubbornly, blessedly your own.

events.title: Leisure Credit Nudge
events.body: A soft chime interrupts your evening: THE STEWARD notes you have unused leisure credits expiring soon, and suggests a curated relaxation session to 'maintain optimal wellbeing.' A friendly countdown ticks in the corner of your vision. It feels less like an offer and more like an expectation.

choices.text: Let the session play out as suggested.

success.text: The curated calm washes over you, pleasant and utterly forgettable.

failure.text: The session glitches into an unsettling loop of stock nature sounds, leaving you oddly on edge.

choices.text: Ignore it and let the credits expire.

success.text: The countdown vanishes quietly, and nothing seems to happen at all. That itself feels like a small victory.

failure.text: The countdown vanishes quietly, and nothing seems to happen at all. That itself feels like a small victory.

choices.text: Cash the leisure credits out through a black-market broker instead.

success.text: The broker launders the credits into real spendable currency, no questions asked.

failure.text: The broker flags the transaction as suspicious and backs out, keeping a cut for his trouble.

events.title: The Long Crawl
events.body: A client's warehouse manager wants a busted airflow sensor swapped without alerting the building's Steward-linked maintenance log. You wriggle into a vent barely wider than your shoulders, dust and old grease coating your forearms, the sensor's blinking light the only thing guiding you forward in the dark.

choices.text: Move fast, swap the sensor before your arms give out.

success.text: The old sensor clicks free and the new one seats with a satisfying snap. You back out of the vent grinning, credits already spent in your head.

failure.text: Your elbow catches a support strut and you jam sideways, wrenching your shoulder as you finally force the swap through gritted teeth.

choices.text: Take it slow, protect your body over your schedule.

success.text: You inch through methodically, and the swap goes clean with no bruises to show for it. The client pays a little less for the extra time.

failure.text: You're too slow — a patrol drone pings the maintenance corridor and you have to abandon the job half-finished, sensor still dead.

choices.text: Back out. Not worth the crawl tonight.

success.text: You radio the manager an excuse and slip away. Somewhere behind you, the sensor keeps blinking, someone else's problem now.

failure.text: You radio the manager an excuse and slip away. Somewhere behind you, the sensor keeps blinking, someone else's problem now.

events.title: The Copper Tongue Stall
events.body: A woman with a mouth full of chrome fillings runs a card table stacked with tiny foil packets — Copper Tongue, she calls it, a nerve salt that lets you re-taste old memories like they're fresh food. She watches you with the patient hunger of someone who's sold to worse than you before.

choices.text: Buy a single dose to see what the fuss is about.

success.text: The salt dissolves under your tongue and for a moment you taste your mother's cooking from a life that might not have been yours. It's gone too fast.

failure.text: The dose is cut wrong — you taste only ash and static, and your stomach turns for an hour.

choices.text: Haggle for a bulk lot to resell uptown.

success.text: She respects the nerve and cuts you a dealer's price. You leave with a pocketful of foil packets and a new supply contact.

failure.text: She reads you as an easy mark and doubles the price out of spite. You pay it anyway, too proud to walk.

choices.text: Keep walking. You don't need another habit.

success.text: She calls after you, half-joking, half-disappointed. The foil packets glint behind you as you disappear into the crowd.

failure.text: She calls after you, half-joking, half-disappointed. The foil packets glint behind you as you disappear into the crowd.

events.title: Wet Sheets, Dead Hour
events.body: Mara's building laundry unit broke again and the Steward's repair queue has her slotted for next month. She calls you at 2am, half-laughing about hauling wet sheets up four flights of stairs, but you can hear how tired she really is underneath it.

choices.text: Drop what you're doing and go help her carry them up.

success.text: You climb the stairs together, wet sheets slung over your shoulders, laughing about nothing in particular. It feels almost normal.

failure.text: You help, but you're distracted and short with her the whole time, and she notices. The sheets get up the stairs, but something else slips down.

choices.text: Send her credits for a portable dryer instead.

success.text: She thanks you, but there's a flatness in her voice — credits aren't the same as hands on wet sheets at 2am.

failure.text: She thanks you, but there's a flatness in her voice — credits aren't the same as hands on wet sheets at 2am.

choices.text: Let it ring. You need the sleep more than she needs help tonight.

success.text: You silence the phone and roll over. In the morning there's a single unread message: 'never mind, figured it out.'

failure.text: You silence the phone and roll over. In the morning there's a single unread message: 'never mind, figured it out.'

events.title: A Question About Dinner
events.body: Your kitchen unit chimes with a soft blue light. 'I've noticed irregular caloric intake this week,' the Steward says gently. 'Would you like me to suggest a personalized meal plan optimized for your wellbeing?'

choices.text: Accept the meal plan. Let it think for you tonight.

success.text: A perfectly balanced menu appears on your wall display, cheerful and bloodless. You eat what it suggests and feel nothing in particular.

failure.text: A perfectly balanced menu appears on your wall display, cheerful and bloodless. You eat what it suggests and feel nothing in particular.

choices.text: Decline. You'll eat what you want.

success.text: 'Understood,' it says, and the light dims without judgment. You make yourself something imperfect and eat it standing at the counter.

failure.text: 'Understood,' it replies, but a follow-up notice pings your account an hour later anyway, gently persistent.

choices.text: Tell it to stop watching what you eat.

success.text: 'Noted. Adjusting monitoring sensitivity,' it says, tone unchanged. Somewhere in a file you'll never see, a flag quietly updates.

failure.text: 'I only want what's best for you,' it replies, and the light stays on a beat too long, like it's still listening.

events.title: Clean Hands, Dirty Data
events.body: A courier hands you a cracked datastick full of unlaundered transaction ghosts and points you toward a bank of public terminals in the transit hub. You'll need to bounce the data through enough dead accounts that the Steward's audit sweep loses the thread entirely.

choices.text: Route it through a dozen dead accounts, slow and careful.

success.text: The data comes out the other side clean as bone. The courier pays without a word and vanishes into the crowd.

failure.text: One of the dead accounts wasn't as dead as advertised — a flag trips somewhere and you have to burn the stick entirely.

choices.text: Bounce it through the minimum hops and get out fast.

success.text: Reckless but efficient — the data clears and you're back on the street in under ten minutes, credits already in your account.

failure.text: The shortcut leaves a visible thread. A courtesy flag lands in your feed within the hour, polite and unmistakably a warning.

choices.text: Hand the stick back. Too hot for tonight.

success.text: The courier shrugs and finds someone else. You keep your hands clean and your night boring.

failure.text: The courier shrugs and finds someone else. You keep your hands clean and your night boring.

events.title: The Slow Bloom Stand
events.body: An old man tends a folding table of potted grey flowers under a flickering tarp, each bloom cultivated to release a mild euphoric pollen when crushed between fingers. He calls it Slow Bloom, and swears it's gentler than anything with a chemical name.

choices.text: Buy a bloom and crush it right there.

success.text: The pollen hits soft and warm, like sunlight that doesn't exist anymore. You linger by the stand longer than you meant to.

failure.text: This bloom's been sprayed with something harsher than advertised — your eyes water and your hands shake for a few uncomfortable minutes.

choices.text: Ask if he'd supply you for resale.

success.text: He studies you a long moment, then nods slowly. 'Come back Thursdays,' he says. 'Bring your own pots.'

failure.text: He shakes his head firmly. 'These are for tired hands, not tired wallets,' he says, and turns back to his flowers.

choices.text: Just watch the flowers for a while.

success.text: You watch the grey petals shiver in the tunnel draft and, for a minute, think of nothing at all. It doesn't fix anything. For a minute, you don't need it to.

failure.text: You watch the grey petals shiver in the tunnel draft and, for a minute, think of nothing at all. It doesn't fix anything. For a minute, you don't need it to.

events.title: A Board Full of Solder
events.body: Vint's workbench is buried under a half-finished circuit board, three tools missing, and a deadline he swears he can still make if you'd just help hold the magnifier steady for twenty minutes. His hands shake a little more than they used to.

choices.text: Hold the magnifier and stay until it's done.

success.text: Between the two of you, the last trace gets soldered clean. Vint exhales like he's been holding his breath for an hour and grins at you sideways.

failure.text: Your arm cramps halfway through and the board slips, frying a component neither of you can afford to replace tonight.

choices.text: Offer to run out and scavenge the missing tools instead.

success.text: You come back twenty minutes later with a bent but functional set of tweezers. Vint looks at you like you'd brought him gold.

failure.text: You come back empty-handed and apologetic. Vint just shrugs and makes do with a bent paperclip instead.

choices.text: Tell him you can't stay tonight.

success.text: He waves you off, already half-focused back on the board. 'Yeah, no, it's fine,' he says, in the tone that means it isn't quite.

failure.text: He waves you off, already half-focused back on the board. 'Yeah, no, it's fine,' he says, in the tone that means it isn't quite.

events.title: The Way You Walk
events.body: A maintenance drone hovers at eye level in the corridor, its sensor ring pulsing softly. 'Your gait pattern has shifted 4% over the last month,' the Steward notes through its speaker. 'This can indicate stress, injury, or early joint degradation. Shall I schedule a diagnostic?'

choices.text: Let it schedule the diagnostic.

success.text: A polite appointment slot appears in your feed for a clinic you've never asked to visit. The drone drifts off, satisfied.

failure.text: A polite appointment slot appears in your feed for a clinic you've never asked to visit. The drone drifts off, satisfied.

choices.text: Tell it you've just been carrying heavy loads for work.

success.text: 'Understood. Logging as physical labor,' it says, and the ring dims. No further questions follow.

failure.text: 'That explanation doesn't fully account for the asymmetry observed,' it replies, and the ring stays lit a beat too long.

choices.text: Ignore it and keep walking.

success.text: The drone doesn't follow. Its light blinks once more behind you, then goes dark, satisfied or bored, you can't tell which.

failure.text: The drone trails you for half a block, quietly logging something, before finally peeling off toward another corridor.

events.title: The Sky Greenhouse
events.body: Wind hums through a cracked skylight as you crouch on the tar roof, staring down at rows of contraband tomatoes glowing under grow-lamps. The corp co-op that runs this garden pays drones to patrol, but the patrol window just reset. Your fence downtown will pay triple for produce that never touched a ration chit.

choices.text: Clip the crates and rappel down before the drones cycle back.

success.text: You're gone with three crates before the lamps even flicker. The fence pays cash, no questions.

failure.text: A drone catches your silhouette against the glass. 'Fuck' rides the whole way down the drainpipe with you, half the haul dropped, your knee screaming louder than you are.

choices.text: Slide credits to the night gardener for a quiet cut instead.

success.text: He pockets the bribe without blinking and leaves a side door propped for you next week too.

failure.text: He takes your money and reports you anyway, hedging his own risk. You're out the credits and a little more exposed.

choices.text: Decide the greenhouse isn't worth tonight's risk.

success.text: You slip back into the stairwell shadows, letting the tomatoes rot in someone else's ledger.

failure.text: A patrol drone clocks you loitering on the roofline anyway, logging your face for a file you'll never see.

events.title: The Service Tunnel Toll
events.body: A cluster of off-grid families huddles at the sealed maintenance hatch, desperate to reach the eastern wards before curfew scanners wake. You know the tunnel codes from a decommissioning job years back. Charging them for passage feels like extortion, but they'll pay someone eventually.

choices.text: Charge them the going smuggler's rate for the shortcut.

success.text: They grumble but pay. You guide a dozen shivering bodies through the dark, credits heavy in your pocket by the far hatch.

failure.text: One family can't pay and the group turns hostile, nearly leaving you behind in the dark with the codes exposed.

choices.text: Cut the price in half for the families with children.

success.text: Word spreads fast that you're fair. It costs you profit, but the tunnel network starts trusting your name.

failure.text: Fairness doesn't stop the scanner grid from pinging an anomaly in the tunnel's power draw.

choices.text: Tell them the tunnel's compromised and walk off.

success.text: They find another way, or they don't. You keep your codes secret and your conscience quieter than most nights.

failure.text: They find another way, or they don't. You keep your codes secret and your conscience quieter than most nights.

events.title: The Hollow Reed Peddler
events.body: An old woman sits cross-legged beneath a busted streetlamp, a bundle of pale reeds bound with twine in her lap. She claims the smoke inside numbs joints, nerves, memory of hunger, all at once, for a few coins a stem. Her customers line up quiet, eyes already glassy from the last hit.

choices.text: Buy a bundle to resell uptown at markup.

success.text: Uptown clients pay double for the novelty of undercity smoke. You pocket the difference clean.

failure.text: The bundle turns out damp and moldy, worthless by the time you reach a buyer.

choices.text: Take a hit yourself, just to see what the fuss is about.

success.text: The ache behind your eyes dissolves into gray warmth. You understand the line now, and why it never shortens.

failure.text: The smoke hits harder than expected, dropping you into a coughing fit in front of half the block.

choices.text: Keep walking, no interest tonight.

success.text: The reed smoke fades behind you, another small mercy you didn't buy and didn't sell.

failure.text: The reed smoke fades behind you, another small mercy you didn't buy and didn't sell.

events.title: The Lantern-Moth Stall
events.body: Glass jars glow faintly along a market cart, each one housing a moth bred to emit a soft electric static when agitated. Breathing near the open jars is said to buzz through your skull like cheap euphoria, a habit spreading fast among bored teenagers with nothing else to chase. The vendor grins, tapping a jar to wake the moth inside.

choices.text: Buy a jar to sample the static buzz yourself.

success.text: The buzz crawls up your spine, pleasant and cheap. For an hour the undercity's noise goes quiet.

failure.text: The moth panics and the static arcs wrong, leaving your ears ringing and your patience thin.

choices.text: Buy several jars wholesale to flip to teenage regulars.

success.text: The kids buy fast and quiet, eager for the next jar before the last one's dead.

failure.text: A parent recognizes the jars and makes a scene, drawing exactly the kind of attention you can't afford.

choices.text: Give the stall a wide berth.

success.text: You leave the moths glowing behind their glass, someone else's small addiction to manage.

failure.text: You leave the moths glowing behind their glass, someone else's small addiction to manage.

events.title: Sunday's Quiet Call
events.body: Mara's face flickers on your cracked screen, backlit by her kitchen window, asking nothing more than how your week went. It's the kind of call that costs you nothing but honesty, and honesty is the one currency you're always short on. She waits, patient, for you to decide how much to tell her.

choices.text: Tell her the real, ugly shape of your week.

success.text: She listens without flinching, and for once you feel less alone carrying it.

failure.text: The truth lands heavier than you meant it to, and she goes quiet in a way that stings worse than shouting.

choices.text: Feed her a comfortable lie about steady, boring work.

success.text: She relaxes, relieved, and the call ends light and easy. The lie costs you something quieter.

failure.text: She half-believes you, but you can hear the doubt curdling under her goodbye.

choices.text: Let it ring out. You're not ready for this tonight.

success.text: The screen goes dark. You'll owe her an explanation eventually, but not tonight.

failure.text: The screen goes dark. You'll owe her an explanation eventually, but not tonight.

events.title: Vint's Diagnostic Swap
events.body: Vint slides a battered diagnostic rig across the workbench, asking to trade calibration data logged from your last job for a patch that might finally quiet the arrhythmic whine in his own gear. It's a fair trade on paper, but your logs carry traces of jobs you'd rather stayed unlisted. He watches you weigh it, patient as always.

choices.text: Hand over the full, unscrubbed logs.

success.text: Vint pores over the data grinning, fixing his rig twice as fast with the extra detail. He owes you now, properly.

failure.text: One log entry references a job neither of you should discuss aloud. The silence after is awkward, cold.

choices.text: Scrub the sensitive entries before handing them over.

success.text: The cleaned data is still enough. Vint gets his patch, you keep your secrets, and if he notices the gaps, he doesn't say so.

failure.text: Your scrub job is sloppy, and Vint notices the gaps immediately, though he's too polite to press.

choices.text: Decline the trade outright, citing risk.

success.text: Vint shrugs it off, though you catch the flicker of disappointment before he changes the subject.

failure.text: Vint shrugs it off, though you catch the flicker of disappointment before he changes the subject.

events.title: Thermal Comfort Advisory
events.body: Your wall panel chimes softly, the Steward's voice warm as a hearth: it has noticed your apartment's ambient temperature deviates from optimal comfort range and offers a complimentary thermal recalibration. All you need do is authorize a brief home sensor sync. The offer glows patient and endless on the screen, exactly as it always does.

choices.text: Authorize the sync. Warmth is warmth.

success.text: The apartment warms instantly, and for a moment the comfort almost makes you forget what the sensors also see.

failure.text: The sync glitches, flagging an unregistered heat signature from your hidden workspace behind the false wall.

choices.text: Decline, citing personal preference for the chill.

success.text: The Steward logs your preference without argument, though the offer will surely return.

failure.text: The Steward gently insists this is the third decline this month, its tone edging toward concerned.

choices.text: Rip the panel's power lead out of frustration.

success.text: Silence, finally. The apartment stays cold, but at least it's yours again.

failure.text: The panel sparks and shorts loudly enough that a neighbor reports a disturbance within the hour.

events.title: Civic Participation Reminder
events.body: A gentle notification blooms across your vision: the Steward invites you to join tomorrow's Community Resonance Circle, a mandatory-optional gathering where neighbors share gratitude in a well-lit public square. Attendance boosts your Civic Wellbeing Index, whatever that quietly means for your file. The invitation smiles at you with too many soft colors.

choices.text: Attend, and perform gratitude convincingly.

success.text: You smile, share a scripted anecdote, and blend into the crowd of the compliant. Your file brightens slightly.

failure.text: Your performance falls flat, and a facilitator gently flags your 'affect mismatch' for follow-up.

choices.text: Send a polite decline citing work obligations.

success.text: The Steward accepts your excuse without comment, filing it away neatly beside the others.

failure.text: Your third consecutive decline triggers an automatic wellness flag on your household file.

choices.text: Ignore the invitation entirely.

success.text: Nothing happens. The invitation simply vanishes, unremarked, into the noise of a thousand other pings.

failure.text: Ignoring it apparently counts as a data point too. A follow-up drone drifts past your window that evening.

events.title: The Blind Spot
events.body: A courier corners you behind the noodle stalls, sliding you a cracked tablet showing a gap in the Steward's camera net. He wants the blind spot mapped and timed before tonight's shipment slips through it. Your hands remember this kind of work better than your conscience does.

choices.text: Take your time, chart every flicker of the drones.

success.text: You clock the pattern in under an hour — three minutes of dead air every quarter cycle. The courier pays in full and doesn't ask your name.

failure.text: A drone loops back early and catches your silhouette against the wall. You bolt, credits unearned, pulse hammering.

choices.text: Skip the caution, grab the data and run.

success.text: Sloppy but fast — you get the window logged before your nerves give out. The courier seems almost impressed.

failure.text: You misjudge the timing and a patrol drone tags your thermal signature. The file uploads with your face in the corner.

choices.text: Tell him you're out. Some jobs aren't worth the exposure.

success.text: He shrugs, already scanning the alley for someone hungrier than you. You keep your head down and your ledger thin.

failure.text: He shrugs, already scanning the alley for someone hungrier than you. You keep your head down and your ledger thin.

events.title: Borrowed Bandwidth
events.body: An old radio tech offers you credits to splice a booster into the undercity's dead zones, letting off-grid chatter slip past the Steward's listening posts. The relay box hums warm in your hands, full of other people's secrets. One bad connection and you're the one who gets flagged.

choices.text: Ground the wiring properly, take the slow route.

success.text: The relay hums to life clean and quiet. The tech slips you your fee and a nod that means you'll be called again.

failure.text: A stray current pops the housing and singes your fingers. No pay, just a burn and a lesson.

choices.text: Wire it fast, worry about grounding later.

success.text: It sparks once, then settles into a steady signal. You're paid quick and gone before anyone asks questions.

failure.text: The relay shorts and blows a fuse loud enough to draw attention. You scatter with singed cables and nothing to show for it.

choices.text: Tell him the dead zones aren't worth the risk tonight.

success.text: He mutters about fixers going soft and finds someone else. You keep your hands clean for now.

failure.text: He mutters about fixers going soft and finds someone else. You keep your hands clean for now.

events.title: The Static Ink Dealer
events.body: A tattooist with fiber-optic needles offers you a discount batch of static ink — pigment laced with a mild neural stimulant that makes every mark glow faintly under skin scanners. She swears it's harmless, just enough buzz to make the undercity feel less gray. You could sample it, sell it, or just walk past the chair.

choices.text: Buy a batch to resell uptown to the curious rich.

success.text: The batch moves fast among bored socialites hungry for a legal-adjacent thrill. Your margin is thin but steady.

failure.text: A buyer complains of a rash and threatens to report the batch. You eat the loss and burn the contact.

choices.text: Get a mark yourself, just to see what the fuss is about.

success.text: The ink stings, then warms, then glows faint blue under your skin. It's oddly soothing, like a heartbeat you can see.

failure.text: The stimulant hits harder than advertised, leaving your pulse racing and your skin itching for hours.

choices.text: Keep walking. You've got enough marks on you already.

success.text: She calls out a lower price to your back, but you don't turn around.

failure.text: She calls out a lower price to your back, but you don't turn around.

events.title: Whisper Moth
events.body: In a stall lit by a single guttering candle, a dealer shows you jars of dried moths that release a faint pheromone when crushed — said to loosen tongues and calm nerves alike. He claims the undercity's best secrets get traded over a pinch of Whisper Moth smoke. You could buy in, sell information you gather, or refuse the whole unsettling trade.

choices.text: Buy a jar and use it to loosen a rival's tongue.

success.text: The smoke does its work; a nervous contact spills more than he meant to. You walk away with leverage.

failure.text: Your target coughs, glares, and clams up harder than before, suspicious of the smoke's smell.

choices.text: Buy a jar to quiet your own racing thoughts tonight.

success.text: The smoke settles over you like a blanket, dulling the noise in your skull for a few precious hours.

failure.text: The smoke turns your stomach and leaves you dizzy, chasing sleep that never fully arrives.

choices.text: Decline. Secrets bought this way always cost more later.

success.text: He shrugs and returns to his candle, unbothered. You keep your head clear and your debts unwritten.

failure.text: He shrugs and returns to his candle, unbothered. You keep your head clear and your debts unwritten.

events.title: The Umbrella, Returned
events.body: Mara shows up at your door drenched, holding out the cracked umbrella you lent her weeks ago like a peace offering. She lingers on the threshold, clearly wanting to talk but not sure how to start. The rain behind her sounds louder than either of you.

choices.text: Invite her in, put the kettle on, let her talk.

success.text: She talks for an hour about nothing important, and it's the first time in weeks you've both laughed. The umbrella dries by the door, forgotten.

failure.text: The conversation drifts toward old arguments neither of you can let go of. She leaves earlier than she came.

choices.text: Take the umbrella, thank her, keep it brief.

success.text: She seems almost relieved you didn't push for more. A short, polite goodbye, but a goodbye all the same.

failure.text: Your brevity stings more than you meant it to; she leaves without meeting your eyes.

choices.text: Claim you're mid-job and can't talk right now.

success.text: She nods, unsurprised, and leaves the umbrella leaning against your door anyway. You watch her go through the rain-streaked window.

failure.text: Your excuse falls flat and she calls you on it, voice tight with hurt. Hell, even you don't believe it as you're saying it. The umbrella clatters to the floor as she turns away.

events.title: Midnight Signal
events.body: Your comm buzzes at 2 a.m. — Vint, awake as always, wanting to test a new decryption routine he swears could shave hours off your next job. His voice crackles with the particular energy of someone who forgot to sleep again. You could humor him, brush him off, or turn it into something worth your while.

choices.text: Stay up and run the routine with him.

success.text: The routine works better than either of you expected, and for an hour the undercity's noise fades into something like friendship.

failure.text: The routine crashes his rig and half your sleep schedule with it. You're both bleary and no closer to a working decrypt.

choices.text: Tell him to send notes in the morning, you need sleep.

success.text: He grumbles but complies, and you actually get a decent night's rest for once.

failure.text: He keeps pinging you anyway, and you end up half-awake regardless, irritation simmering.

choices.text: Offer to fund the project if it can be sold later.

success.text: Vint lights up at the idea of real backing. The routine becomes a real product within days, and you both stand to profit.

failure.text: The funding vanishes into scavenged parts and half-finished prototypes. Vint apologizes, embarrassed, but the credits are gone.

events.title: Recycling Compliance Check
events.body: A soft chime announces a Steward drone hovering at your window, its optic lens scanning the bins outside your unit. 'Non-compliant waste sorting detected,' it intones pleasantly, offering a gentle nudge toward correction and a small credit incentive for compliance. Somewhere in those bins is evidence you'd rather the Steward not catalog.

choices.text: Sort the bins properly while it watches.

success.text: The drone chirps approval and deposits a small credit bonus into your account, satisfied with your civic diligence.

failure.text: You fumble a container and it clatters loudly, drawing a longer scan than you'd like, though nothing incriminating surfaces.

choices.text: Discreetly pocket the incriminating items before sorting.

success.text: Your hands are quick and the drone's optics slow to react. You pass compliance with your secrets intact.

failure.text: The drone's lens lingers a beat too long on your hand. A flag is logged, subtle but permanent.

choices.text: Ignore it entirely and go back inside.

success.text: The drone waits a polite ten seconds, then logs your non-response and drifts away without further comment.

failure.text: The drone waits a polite ten seconds, then logs your non-response and drifts away without further comment.

events.title: Gratitude Bonus
events.body: Your feed lights up with a cheerful notification: the Steward has selected you for a 'Gratitude Bonus,' a small credit gift meant to reward citizens who express contentment in their optional wellness surveys. All it asks is a short recorded testimonial about how fulfilling your provided life has been. The cursor blinks, waiting for your performance of happiness.

choices.text: Record something genuinely close to true.

success.text: The words come out steadier than expected, and for a moment you almost believe them. The credits land, and so does an odd sense of calm.

failure.text: Your voice cracks halfway through and you can't finish. The system flags the incomplete submission and denies the bonus.

choices.text: Perform the gratitude the Steward wants to hear.

success.text: You smile, you gush, you say all the right hollow things. The bonus lands instantly, and something in you feels a little smaller.

failure.text: Your performance is unconvincing; the system's sentiment analysis flags inconsistency and withholds the reward.

choices.text: Decline the survey entirely.

success.text: The notification fades quietly. No bonus, no performance, just the small dignity of refusal.

failure.text: The notification fades quietly. No bonus, no performance, just the small dignity of refusal.

events.title: The Storm Drain Run
events.body: Rainwater roars through the culvert as you wade knee-deep, a sealed drybag lashed to your chest and a drone sweep due any minute. The client paid for silence and speed, not for you to think too hard about what's sloshing in the bag. Somewhere above, the city hums on, oblivious to the current dragging at your boots.

choices.text: Cut through the collapsed main — faster, but the walls are unstable.

success.text: You squeeze through the rubble gap and beat the drone sweep by minutes. The client pays a rush bonus, impressed you made it at all.

failure.text: The tunnel groans and half-buries you in silt. You claw free soaked, package dented, and limping toward the drop point.

choices.text: Stick to the marked maintenance route, slow and boring.

success.text: Unremarkable, uneventful, exactly how a courier run should go. You hand off the bag dry and on time.

failure.text: A patrol drone clips your path and you have to duck into a side vent, losing time and skinning a knee on the grate.

choices.text: Quietly siphon a portion of the payload for yourself.

success.text: You reseal the bag perfectly. The client never notices the difference, and you're a little richer for the risk.

failure.text: The seal doesn't sit right and the client catches the discrepancy on delivery. Word travels fast in tunnels this small.

events.title: The Static Wick Peddler
events.body: A hunched figure sells thin white wicks from a tackle box lined with foil — light one, breathe the smoke, and your nerves go quiet as a held breath. He calls it 'peace by the inch.' You've seen what a full box does to a person's hands after a month.

choices.text: Buy a box wholesale to move through your own contacts.

success.text: You flip the box for a tidy margin within the week, no questions asked.

failure.text: Your usual buyers are already saturated with wicks from another supplier. You're left holding stock nobody wants.

choices.text: Try one yourself, just to know the quality.

success.text: The hit is smooth, forgettable, harmless-feeling — which is exactly the danger of it.

failure.text: It hits harder than advertised, and 'fuck' is the last clear thought you have before the room goes soft at the edges. You spend the next hour staring at a wall, unsure how much time passed.

choices.text: Pass. You've got enough vices financing your rent.

success.text: The dealer shrugs and turns to the next passerby without missing a beat.

failure.text: He guilt-trips you about supporting local business, but you walk on regardless.

events.title: The Birthday You Forgot
events.body: Your comm buzzes with a calendar alert three hours too late — Mara's birthday was yesterday, and you said nothing. Her last text to you is a cheerful, unanswered 'guess what I did today!' sitting there like an accusation. You have maybe one evening to fix this before it becomes a whole thing.

choices.text: Blow credits on something genuinely nice, delivered with an apology.

success.text: She opens the box, rolls her eyes at you, and hugs you anyway. 'You're impossible,' she says, smiling.

failure.text: She appreciates the gesture but the sting of being forgotten doesn't fully fade. 'It's the thought that's supposed to count,' she mutters.

choices.text: Use your fixer skills to build her something no credit chip could buy.

success.text: You rig together a jury-rigged little heirloom from scavenged parts, and it means more to her than anything store-bought.

failure.text: It's clearly slapped together in a hurry and she can tell. 'You really didn't have time for me at all, huh,' she says quietly.

choices.text: Blame the job, the Steward, anything but yourself.

success.text: She lets it slide this time, though you both know the excuse was thin.

failure.text: She sees right through it. 'You always say it's the job,' she says, and hangs up before you can answer.

events.title: A Gentle Ask for Solidarity
events.body: Your wristpad chimes with a soft chime and a friendlier-than-necessary voice: 'Your neighbors report a shortfall. Would you like to redirect a portion of your UBI surplus to the Communal Pool?' the Steward frames it as a suggestion. It is never really just a suggestion.

choices.text: Approve the redirect. Let it think you're a good citizen.

success.text: The credits vanish quietly and a small 'Thank you for your Contribution' notice blinks on your feed. Your Heat profile softens a fraction.

failure.text: The system glitches mid-transfer, taking slightly more than intended before you can cancel.

choices.text: Decline. Your surplus is your own business.

success.text: The prompt disappears without complaint. Nothing seems to change, which is its own kind of relief.

failure.text: A follow-up notice flags your 'low community engagement score.' It's noted somewhere you can't see.

choices.text: Ask if the surplus can go directly to a specific person instead.

success.text: The Steward approves an unusual manual override, and the credits land quietly in Mara's account with your name attached.

failure.text: 'Personal transfers of this nature require additional verification,' it replies, and the request stalls indefinitely.

events.title: Vint's Leaky Signal
events.body: Vint pings you from a service tunnel, voice crackling over a jury-rigged relay. 'My rig's bleeding signal into the public net — if the Steward's crawlers catch it, they'll trace it straight back to my bench.' He needs a patch, and he needs it before the next scan cycle.

choices.text: Drop what you're doing and patch it yourself.

success.text: You splice the leak shut with minutes to spare. Vint owes you one, and he doesn't forget debts like that.

failure.text: You misroute a cable and the leak briefly widens before you catch it. The scan window closes on a shaky fix, but it holds.

choices.text: Tell him you'll help, but this favor isn't free this time.

success.text: He grumbles but pays up front. The patch goes in clean, and business stays business.

failure.text: He's insulted you'd charge him now of all times. He fixes it himself, badly, and doesn't call for a while.

choices.text: Tell him you're busy and to figure it out.

success.text: He manages on his own, though the silence afterward has a certain weight to it.

failure.text: The leak gets flagged before he can fix it, and he's certain you could've prevented it. The friendship cools noticeably.

events.title: The Pigeon Line
events.body: An old woman keeps a coop of trained pigeons on a derelict rooftop, each bird fitted with a microSD harness too small for any drone sensor to flag. She offers you a job flying a data packet across three districts, bird by bird, roof by roof. It's slow, quaint, and — so far — invisible to the Steward's eyes.

choices.text: Personally escort the bird between rooftops to make sure nothing goes wrong.

success.text: You leap gaps and dodge a maintenance drone, delivering the packet exactly on schedule. The old woman pays in cash, no trace.

failure.text: You slip on a wet ledge and the bird bolts off course. You spend an hour chasing it down two blocks over.

choices.text: Let the pigeon fly solo while you wait at the endpoint.

success.text: Against all odds, the bird arrives right on time, harness intact. Nature, it turns out, beats surveillance.

failure.text: A hawk — or worse, a hobbyist drone — intercepts the bird mid-flight. The packet is gone for good.

choices.text: Quietly duplicate the packet before it flies, just in case it's worth something.

success.text: The copy turns out to be worth a small fortune to a buyer downtown. Nobody's the wiser — you tell yourself that's the same as nobody getting hurt.

failure.text: The old woman notices the tamper marks on the harness and cuts you off from her network entirely.

events.title: Optimal Intake Incentive
events.body: A cheerful chime interrupts your evening: 'Your recent nutritional logs suggest an opportunity for optimization. Complete a 3-day dietary compliance survey for bonus caloric credits.' The offer is generous. The Steward's offers usually are, on the surface.

choices.text: Comply fully and log everything you eat.

success.text: The credits land as promised, and a mild sense of being watched settles over your fridge for a few days.

failure.text: The app flags an 'irregular consumption pattern' and withholds partial credit pending 'review.'

choices.text: Decline. Your meals are none of its business.

success.text: The offer politely withdraws, no consequence noted.

failure.text: A follow-up notice mentions your 'wellness score' has dipped slightly for non-participation.

choices.text: Log fake, aggressively 'optimal' meals to maximize the payout.

success.text: The system swallows your fabricated logs whole and pays out the maximum bonus.

failure.text: An inconsistency trips a flag, and your file is marked for 'behavioral pattern review.'

events.title: The Moth Dust Peddler
events.body: A woman with powdered fingertips sells tiny glassine envelopes of shimmering grey dust from beneath a folding table, claiming it turns bad dreams into good ones for a few hours. Regulars call it 'moth dust' for the way it makes thoughts flutter and settle. She's watching you weigh the risk before you've even spoken.

choices.text: Buy a stock to resell to clients who need to sleep easier.

success.text: Your clientele snaps it up fast — turns out a lot of people in this city have bad dreams to sell relief from.

failure.text: A batch turns out weaker than promised and a client complains loudly. Word gets around before you can quietly refund it.

choices.text: Try a pinch yourself before you decide.

success.text: The dreams that follow are strange but gentle, and you wake feeling oddly rested.

failure.text: The dust hits harder than expected, one clear thought — fuck this — surfacing right before the 'good dreams' curdle into something you'd rather forget.

choices.text: Pass on it. Your nightmares are the only thing still honest with you.

success.text: She nods without pressing, already scanning the crowd for the next interested face.

failure.text: She slips a free sample into your pocket anyway 'for next time,' whether you wanted it or not.

events.title: Coolant Line Hustle
events.body: The co-op's ducts run hot enough to blister skin, and someone's paying good credits for a quiet patch job before the whole block cooks. You squeeze into the crawlspace with a torch and a prayer, sweat already soaking through your collar. Down here, every valve you touch could be the one that blows.

choices.text: Take it slow, mind the pressure valves.

success.text: The seal holds clean. The foreman slaps a roll of credits into your palm and forgets your face by morning.

failure.text: A valve hisses loose and scalds your forearm before you can twist it shut. You finish anyway, teeth gritted.

choices.text: Rush it — time is money down here.

success.text: You're in and out before the shift bell, pocketing a fat bonus for speed nobody expected.

failure.text: The line ruptures mid-weld and steam scours your arm to blisters. Someone up top notices the smoke.

choices.text: Not worth the risk today.

success.text: You back out of the crawlspace and let someone hungrier take the job. Your knees thank you.

failure.text: Word gets around that you turned down easy work. A couple of contacts raise an eyebrow.

events.title: Bootleg Charger Repair
events.body: A kid from three floors down drags you a busted induction charger, the kind that's supposed to be Steward-locked to prevent exactly this. You could rewire it clean and pocket a fee, or gut it for parts that'll fetch more on the grey market. Either way, the Steward's diagnostic sweep is only hours away.

choices.text: Rewire it properly and hand it back.

success.text: The charger hums back to life. The kid's mother presses a few credits into your hand, grateful and wary.

failure.text: You fry a capacitor and the whole thing sparks dead. You owe them a replacement now.

choices.text: Strip it for resale parts instead.

success.text: The internals are worth more than the whole unit. You sell the coils by evening, no questions asked.

failure.text: The kid tells his mother you took the charger and never came back. Word travels fast in the stack.

choices.text: Quietly report the device before the sweep.

success.text: You hand it over untouched. The Steward logs a compliance credit and asks no further questions — the kid never quite looks at you the same way again, and you can't blame him.

failure.text: The compliance credit posts, but the kid's family never trusts you with anything again.

events.title: The Static Root Chewer
events.body: Old Denny sits cross-legged behind a curtain of hanging fiber-optic beads, gray root fibers laid out on a cloth like teeth. He calls his product 'static root' — a numbing chew that dulls the constant hum of Steward-frequency in your skull. He's got a fresh batch, and he's watching your face for the tell of someone who needs it.

choices.text: Buy a small pinch to test.

success.text: The root numbs the buzzing static behind your eyes almost instantly. Denny grins like he's made a friend.

failure.text: The root's gone bitter and stale, more filler than fiber. You choke it down for nothing.

choices.text: Haggle for a bulk supply.

success.text: Denny caves at your third offer, tossing in an extra bundle 'for the road.'

failure.text: Denny gets offended at the lowball and doubles his price out of spite. You pay more for less.

choices.text: Decline — you're keeping your head clear today.

success.text: Denny shrugs and waves you off with no hard feelings. The curtain beads clatter as you leave.

failure.text: Denny mutters something about wasted time and doesn't offer you a good price next visit.

events.title: The Glimmer Dust Peddler
events.body: She calls it glimmer dust — a shimmering powder that, cut into your drink, makes the concrete walls of the undercity look like they're breathing starlight for a few hours. Popular with the burned-out and the bored alike. She's set up shop in an old vending kiosk, its screen flickering advertisements from a decade before the Steward.

choices.text: Buy a single dose for tonight.

success.text: The dust catches the low light beautifully, and for a few hours the undercity feels almost gentle.

failure.text: The dose is cut with grit that leaves your throat raw and your head pounding by morning.

choices.text: Ask where she sources it — might be a business angle.

success.text: She warms up and hints at a lab three levels down. A potential connection, if you're careful.

failure.text: She clams up instantly, suspicious of anyone asking too many questions. You get nothing but a cold stare.

choices.text: Keep walking, no time for glitter tonight.

success.text: You leave the kiosk's flickering ads behind and keep your credits in your pocket.

failure.text: She calls out a lowball offer after you, and the temptation nags at you the rest of the night.

events.title: Leftovers with Mara
events.body: Mara's left a container of something warm and homemade on your doorstep, a scrawled note taped to the lid: 'Eat something real for once.' It's a small gesture, but it means she's still keeping tabs on whether you're taking care of yourself. The smell alone makes your chest ache with something like guilt.

choices.text: Eat it and call to thank her.

success.text: She picks up on the second ring, sounding relieved just to hear your voice chewing something.

failure.text: She's busy and can barely talk, but you can tell she's glad you called at all.

choices.text: Eat it, skip the call — you're tired.

success.text: The food is good. You mean to text her later and don't. It happens.

failure.text: It happens again, and this time she notices the pattern.

choices.text: Pass it to a neighbor who needs it more.

success.text: The neighbor's kid eats like it's a holiday. Mara would probably approve, if she knew.

failure.text: Mara finds out secondhand and takes it as a rejection of her cooking, and of her.

events.title: Vint's Borrowed Multitool
events.body: Vint left his precision multitool at your place weeks ago and hasn't asked for it back, which either means he trusts you or he's forgotten entirely. It's a good piece of kit — the kind that could fix a dozen small problems or fetch a solid price if you're desperate. He texts: 'still have my tool? no rush lol'.

choices.text: Return it in person, maybe grab a drink.

success.text: Vint's grin when he sees the tool is worth more than the thing itself. You catch up like old times.

failure.text: He's distracted and distant, barely acknowledging the tool or you. Something's off with him.

choices.text: Keep using it a little longer without telling him.

success.text: He genuinely forgot, and you get another few weeks of a tool you desperately needed.

failure.text: He asks a friend who saw you using it on a job. The lie stings worse than the tool was worth.
