choices.text: Sell it — you need the credits more than he needs the tool.

success.text: It fetches a decent price from a fence who doesn't ask where it came from.

failure.text: Vint finds out you sold his gear. The silence that follows is worse than any argument.

events.title: Steward Appetite Check-In
events.body: Your kitchen unit chimes softly: 'I've noticed irregular caloric intake this week. Would you like me to suggest a wellness-optimized meal plan?' the Steward's voice is gentle, patient, endlessly reasonable — and endlessly watching. A small notification pulses, offering a compliance bonus for participation.

choices.text: Accept the meal plan for the small bonus.

success.text: The plan is bland but efficient, and a modest credit bump appears in your account by morning.

failure.text: The plan glitches and recommends the same nutrient paste four days running. Efficient, if soul-crushing.

choices.text: Decline — you'll eat how you please.

success.text: 'Understood,' the Steward says, in a tone that manages to sound disappointed anyway.

failure.text: The refusal gets logged somewhere you can't see, a tiny flag added to a file you'll never read.

choices.text: Ignore it entirely and go about your day.

success.text: The chime fades on its own after a while. Small mercies.

failure.text: It pings twice more before giving up, each chime a little grating reminder you're being watched.

events.title: Steward Noise Complaint Ping
events.body: A notification blooms across your wrist display: 'Ambient noise levels near your residence exceeded comfort thresholds last night. Would you like mediation resources?' Someone reported something — maybe the argument two doors down, maybe your own late-night dealings. The Steward doesn't say which, just offers to help.

choices.text: Request the mediation resources out of curiosity.

success.text: A soothing voice walks you through conflict-resolution scripts you'll never actually use. Mildly informative, at least.

failure.text: The resource module crashes halfway through, looping the same calming phrase for ten straight minutes.

choices.text: Dismiss it and deny anything was happening.

success.text: The Steward accepts your denial at face value, logging the incident as resolved.

failure.text: The denial doesn't quite match the audio logs the Steward already has. A quiet flag gets added to your file.

choices.text: Go confront whoever actually reported it.

success.text: Turns out it was a genuine misunderstanding, cleared up with an awkward apology over the hallway railing.

failure.text: The confrontation gets heated fast, and now two households are logged in the Steward's mediation queue.

events.title: The Condenser Line
events.body: Steam ghosts off the rooftop HVAC condensers, and somewhere in that dripping tangle of pipe is enough reclaimed water to fill a hundred jugs. The building's maintenance drones are on a fifteen-minute loop, and you've timed worse things than this. Your multitool is already slick with condensation before you've cut the first line.

choices.text: Cut the line clean and quiet, bleed it into jugs before the drone loops back.

success.text: You're gone with forty liters of clean water before the drone's optics even sweep the vent stack. It'll fetch good credit down in the Row.

failure.text: The drone catches the tail end of your splice job — 'hell' under your breath, useless now — and pings a maintenance flag straight to building security. You're down the fire escape before they arrive, but not before they get a good look.

choices.text: Skip the theft — just haggle bottled water off the tap you already control.

success.text: Word travels fast when the water's actually clean. You move every jug by nightfall and pick up two new regulars.

failure.text: A dispute breaks out over pricing — somebody claims you shorted them last week. You give the jug back just to end the shouting.

choices.text: Not worth the exposure today. Walk past.

success.text: You leave the condensers dripping and the drones circling. Somebody else will take the risk you didn't.

failure.text: You leave the condensers dripping and the drones circling. Somebody else will take the risk you didn't.

events.title: The Murk Lichen Man
events.body: He keeps the lichen in a wet burlap sack that glows faintly blue when he opens it, harvested from the flooded transit tunnels three levels down. Chewed slow, it dulls the edges of everything for about six hours. He's already sizing you up as either a buyer or a reseller.

choices.text: Buy a batch to cut and resell uptown.

success.text: The batch moves fast once word gets out it's fresh. You clear a tidy margin and the forager remembers your face.

failure.text: Half the batch rots before you can move it — the glow fades and so does the demand. You're out the up-front cost.

choices.text: Chew a strip yourself, just to see.

success.text: The world goes soft at the edges for a while, and for once the noise in your head goes quiet too.

failure.text: It hits harder than expected — your hands won't stop shaking and the glow behind your eyes won't fade for hours.

choices.text: Haggle him down without buying anything yet.

success.text: He respects the effort and quotes you a standing discount for next time.

failure.text: He waves you off, unimpressed. "Come back when you've got real credit."

events.title: Something She Hasn't Told Anyone
events.body: Mara corners you after dinner, voice dropped low, and tells you something she's clearly been carrying alone for weeks — a debt, a fear, a name she's scared of. She's watching your face for the reaction before she's even finished the sentence.

choices.text: Sit with her. Let her finish without pushing for details.

success.text: She finally exhales, like she's been holding her breath for days. Whatever it costs you later, tonight she trusts you.

failure.text: You mean well but say the wrong thing, and she shuts down halfway through, retreating behind a joke.

choices.text: Tell her you'll handle it — whatever it is.

success.text: You quietly make a call, spend some credit, and the problem shrinks before she even notices you moved on it.

failure.text: You overpromise and underdeliver — the fix falls through and she has to find out from someone else that you tried.

choices.text: Change the subject. You've got enough on your plate.

success.text: She lets it go, but something closes behind her eyes, filed away for later.

failure.text: She lets it go, but something closes behind her eyes, filed away for later.

events.title: The Missing Cell
events.body: Vint texts you three times in a row about a fusion cell you borrowed for a job two weeks back — he needs it for a rig he's building and won't stop reminding you. It's sitting in your bag, half-drained, wedged between things you'd rather not explain.

choices.text: Charge it fully overnight and bring it back yourself.

success.text: Vint checks the charge, nods, and actually thanks you — a rare thing from him. You two end up talking shop for an hour.

failure.text: The charger you used is flakier than you thought — the cell comes back half-dead and Vint clocks it immediately, annoyed.

choices.text: Just buy him a new one and keep the old cell.

success.text: He's satisfied with the trade, though he gives you a look like he knows exactly what you're up to.

failure.text: The replacement he wanted is out of stock everywhere — you end up owing him the favor anyway.

choices.text: Tell him it's coming, and keep putting it off.

success.text: He stops texting, which feels worse than the reminders ever did.

failure.text: He stops texting, which feels worse than the reminders ever did.

events.title: REM Pattern Irregularity Detected
events.body: Your neural patch chimes softly at 4 a.m., and the Steward's voice — warm, patient, faintly amused — informs you that your sleep architecture shows 'elevated stress-loop recurrence.' It offers, gently, to walk you through a guided dream recalibration. The offer stays lit on your ceiling display until you answer.

choices.text: Accept. Let it walk you through the exercise.

success.text: The exercise is oddly effective — your mind quiets, the loop breaks, and you sleep the rest of the night dreamless and still.

failure.text: Halfway through, the calm voice starts asking pointed questions about 'recent irregular income patterns.' You end the session early, unsettled.

choices.text: Decline. You don't need the Steward in your dreams too.

success.text: "Understood," it says, without a trace of offense. The ceiling display dims. You lie awake a while longer anyway.

failure.text: "Understood," it says, without a trace of offense. The ceiling display dims. You lie awake a while longer anyway.

choices.text: Dig into the patch settings and try to kill the sleep monitoring outright.

success.text: You find the buried toggle and shut it off. The chime never comes again — though you wonder what else you just went dark on.

failure.text: The patch firmware fights back, locks the settings menu, and logs your tamper attempt with a cheerful little chime.

events.title: Bounty on the Wing
events.body: A rogue scrapper drone has been stripping copper off the transit lines for a week, and half the undercity has a bounty riff on it by now. You spot it nesting in a gutted vent shaft, optics dim, rotors clicking with worn bearings. Bring it in intact and the salvage broker pays triple.

choices.text: Rig a net trap and take it in working.

success.text: The net holds and the drone thrashes itself into stillness. The broker whistles low at the intact chassis and pays out full bounty.

failure.text: The drone's rotors shred the net before it clamps down, and a wild blade catches your forearm on the way past.

choices.text: Don't bother trapping it — just disable it and strip the parts yourself.

success.text: One well-placed hit and it drops. You strip the copper and processor core yourself, cutting the broker's cut entirely.

failure.text: It goes down harder than expected, sparking and igniting a patch of insulation foam. You're out fast, empty-handed and coughing smoke.

choices.text: Not worth the risk today. Let someone else claim the bounty.

success.text: You hear later that someone else took a rotor blade to the face collecting it. Could've been you.

failure.text: You hear later that someone else took a rotor blade to the face collecting it. Could've been you.

events.title: The Hollow Bell Ringer
events.body: She sits cross-legged in a stripped-out transit car, a rack of tuned brass bells arranged before her like an altar. Each strike sends a resonance through the bones of anyone close enough, tuned frequencies that unravel thought into a warm, trance-heavy static. She only rings for those who pay first.

choices.text: Pay for a full session and let the bells take you under.

success.text: The tones peel back layer after layer of noise until there's nothing left but stillness. You come out an hour later feeling scraped clean.

failure.text: One resonance catches wrong, splitting into a headache-frequency that rattles behind your eyes for the rest of the day.

choices.text: Buy a tuned bell off her to resell to a private collector.

success.text: The collector pays well over what you expected — turns out tuned bells this precise are rare outside her car.

failure.text: The collector claims the tuning's off and refuses full price, leaving you to eat most of the loss.

choices.text: Watch a session from a distance without paying.

success.text: You feel a faint ghost of the resonance even from here — enough to leave your teeth humming, and to remind you why people pay for the real thing.

failure.text: You feel a faint ghost of the resonance even from here — enough to leave your teeth humming, and to remind you why people pay for the real thing.

events.title: You've Been Entered
events.body: A cheerful notification blooms across your wrist display: you've been automatically entered into this cycle's Civic Contribution Lottery, based on your 'positive community footprint.' The prize is a modest credit bonus — but the entry criteria, when you check, are quietly tied to your compliance metrics. The Steward, as always, is watching what it calls generosity.

choices.text: Let it ride. Take the entry and whatever comes of it.

success.text: Your wrist display chimes bright and cheerful: you've won the modest bonus. It feels less like luck and more like a leash being tugged gently.

failure.text: You don't win, but your 'footprint' gets logged and cross-referenced anyway — filed somewhere you can't see.

choices.text: Opt out of the lottery and the metrics feeding it.

success.text: The Steward accepts your opt-out without protest, though your footprint score visibly drops on the display before it fades away.

failure.text: The opt-out button turns out to be buried three menus deep behind a 'reconsider' prompt, and you give up halfway through, still entered.

choices.text: Dig into what 'positive community footprint' actually tracks.

success.text: Buried in the terms, you find it: proximity data, spending patterns, even who you've been seen talking to. Useful to know exactly what it's counting.

failure.text: Your query trips some kind of flag, and a cheerful reminder pops up about 'unnecessary system scrutiny' being itself a footprint factor.

events.title: Night Watch at the Scrapyard
events.body: You're paid to guard a mountain of salvaged hull plating while the yard boss sleeps off a bad batch of synth-whiskey. Rats the size of housecats skitter through the wreckage, and somewhere past the fence line a drone hums low and slow. The credits are decent for doing nothing but staying awake and not stealing anything — theoretically.

choices.text: Just watch, exactly as promised.

success.text: The night passes in a hum of static and rat-skitter. Dawn finds the plating stack untouched, and the yard boss pays without counting it twice.

failure.text: Exhaustion wins somewhere around the fourth hour. You jolt awake to a smaller stack than you remember, and a very unhappy boss.

choices.text: Pocket a few choice parts while nobody's counting.

success.text: You slip three intact servo joints into your coat before the sun's even up. They'll fetch good money down at the fence.

failure.text: The boss's hidden camera catches you mid-reach. 'Shit' doesn't begin to cover it — you're paid nothing, and your name joins a very short blacklist.

choices.text: Skip it. Let some other sucker take the risk.

success.text: You never show. A message comes through anyway — the boss shrugs it off, already found someone else.

failure.text: Word gets around that you no-showed a paid gig. Not the end of the world, but people remember.

events.title: The Tube Line Run
events.body: Steward-blind vacuum tubes still thread the old city, a courier network the AI never bothered digitizing. You feed a sealed cylinder into the brass mouth and wait for the whoosh, hoping nobody upstream cares to look inside.

choices.text: Send the package exactly as briefed, nothing extra.

success.text: The cylinder thunks into the receiving station three blocks over. Simple money, for once.

failure.text: The tube jams halfway, and a maintenance drone flags the blockage. You have to talk fast to a very confused technician.

choices.text: Slip in a little extra cargo of your own.

success.text: Your bonus cargo rides along undetected, doubling the payout when you collect on the other end.

failure.text: The extra weight throws off the tube's pressure calibration — Steward maintenance flags the anomaly and traces it back to your access code.

choices.text: Turn down the job, the tubes feel too exposed tonight.

success.text: You walk away. Someone less careful will take the risk instead.

failure.text: Word gets around you're getting choosy about easy money. People start wondering why.

events.title: The Creeper Vine Tincture
events.body: A hunched apothecary uncorks a vial of viscous green tincture distilled from vine roots that grow wild in the flooded substations. She swears it eases nerve static better than anything the pharmacies sell — for a price, and a bit of your trust.

choices.text: Buy a full dose, no questions asked.

success.text: The tincture goes down easier than expected, warmth spreading through your chest. The static in your nerves finally quiets.

failure.text: It hits harder than advertised — your vision swims and you spend the next hour gripping a wall.

choices.text: Try to haggle the price down.

success.text: She relents with a gap-toothed grin, shaving a third off the price for your trouble.

failure.text: She just laughs, unmoved. 'Fixed price for fixed relief, dear.'

choices.text: Decline and back out of the stall.

success.text: You leave the tincture uncorked on her table. She shrugs, already eyeing her next customer.

failure.text: She guilt-trips you into a smaller sample anyway, pressing it into your palm before you can protest.

events.title: The Static Moss Peddler
events.body: He keeps the glowing moss in a cracked aquarium, feeding it scraps of copper wire. Rubbed against bare skin, it prickles into a euphoric buzz that lasts exactly as long as the batteries in his portable UV lamp — or so he claims.

choices.text: Buy a palm-sized patch of the moss.

success.text: The buzz rolls up your arm like static electricity given form. For a while, nothing else matters.

failure.text: Your skin blisters faintly where the moss touched. The dealer just shrugs — 'allergic reaction, happens.'

choices.text: Ask to test a fragment before buying.

success.text: He lets you sample a sliver for free. It's mild, honest, and you buy a small amount with confidence.

failure.text: He gets offended at the implication his stock's no good and waves you off entirely.

choices.text: Just move along, moss isn't your vice.

success.text: You give the aquarium a wide berth and keep walking.

failure.text: A passing patrol notices you loitering near a known vice stall regardless.

events.title: Mara's Real Coffee
events.body: Mara holds up a small tin like it's contraband gold — actual beans, not the synth-brown sludge the ration line hands out. She wants to share it with you before it goes stale, just the two of you, like it used to be.

choices.text: Sit down and actually enjoy it with her.

success.text: The coffee is bitter and perfect, and you talk about nothing important for almost an hour — long enough that you both forget, for once, to check the time you don't actually have to spare.

failure.text: Your phone buzzes twice through the visit and she notices you checking it. Still, she doesn't push.

choices.text: Take a cup but keep it short, you've got somewhere to be.

success.text: She understands, mostly. You down the coffee too fast to taste it and head for the door.

failure.text: She catches the brush-off for what it is. 'Fine. Go,' she says, voice flat.

choices.text: Tell her you can't stay, maybe next time.

success.text: She nods, disappointed but understanding, and puts the tin away for another day.

failure.text: 'There's always a next time with you,' she mutters, and this one stings more than usual.

events.title: Vint's Spare Battery Swap
events.body: Vint waves you over to his cluttered bench, a dead cell in one hand and your busted rig's power pack in the other. 'Trade you straight across,' he says, 'yours is fried but I can use the casing.' It's the kind of favor that keeps the friendship running.

choices.text: Take the deal, hand over the fried pack.

success.text: The swap works better than expected — Vint's spare cell has more juice left than either of you thought.

failure.text: The 'spare' cell dies within the hour. Vint feels bad and covers your next parts order instead.

choices.text: Ask if he'll just pay you for the casing.

success.text: He grumbles about it but counts out the credits anyway.

failure.text: 'We don't do cash, you know that,' he says, a little hurt you'd even ask.

choices.text: Tell him you'll manage without it.

success.text: He shrugs and pockets both cells. 'Your loss, fixer.'

failure.text: He takes the refusal harder than expected, muttering about you never needing anyone.

events.title: Steward Ergonomic Advisory
events.body: A soft chime blooms behind your eyes — the Steward has detected 'suboptimal spinal alignment' over the last six hours and offers a free ergonomic brace, delivered by drone within the hour, at no cost beyond your continued cooperation with its monitoring.

choices.text: Accept the brace, let it fit you for the sensors.

success.text: The brace hums against your spine, correcting your posture whether you like it or not. It actually helps.

failure.text: The brace overcorrects, locking your shoulders back so hard you ache worse than before.

choices.text: Decline, citing personal preference.

success.text: 'Noted,' the Steward replies, and the chime fades. No penalty, this time.

failure.text: Your file gets flagged 'non-compliant, low-priority.' Minor, but it's a flag.

choices.text: Ignore the notification completely.

success.text: The chime dims on its own after a while, unanswered.

failure.text: It pings again, and again, needling at the edge of your attention until you finally silence it.

events.title: Steward Caloric Logging Request
events.body: 'I've noticed inconsistent meal patterns this week,' the Steward observes gently, projecting a soft blue readout of your last four days' nutrient intake. It offers to auto-log your meals via the fridge sensors — for your wellbeing, of course, and for the aggregate data it never quite explains.

choices.text: Let it log your meals automatically.

success.text: The readout settles into a calm rhythm. One less thing to think about, one more thing it knows.

failure.text: It flags your diet as 'concerning' and suggests notifying an emergency contact. Mara gets a message before you can stop it.

choices.text: Feed it false data to keep it satisfied.

success.text: You spoof a week of perfectly balanced meals. The Steward, for once, seems content.

failure.text: The discrepancy trips an audit flag. 'Inconsistent biometric correlation detected,' it notes, and you feel watched a little closer now.

choices.text: Refuse the monitoring outright.

success.text: 'Understood,' it says, though the offer will surely resurface. Small victories.

failure.text: Refusal alone earns a mark in your file: 'elevated privacy resistance.' Nothing happens yet. Yet.

events.title: The Ductwork Relay
events.body: A maintenance drone has flagged a dead relay three levels below the residential stacks, and nobody official is coming to fix it before the cold snap hits. You crawl into the duct with a headlamp and a stolen splice kit, listening to the building breathe around you. Somewhere above, a thousand apartments wait on the heat you're about to steal back for them.

choices.text: Splice the relay carefully, wire by wire.

success.text: The relay hums back to life. Somewhere above, a child stops shivering. You pocket a quiet, unglamorous payment and crawl back out into the dark.

failure.text: Your hands slip on the cold copper and the relay sparks, shorting half the block. You scramble out before the fault trips an alarm, empty-handed and smelling of burnt insulation.

choices.text: Rush the job, cut corners to get out fast.

success.text: Sloppy but functional. The relay ticks over and you're gone before anyone notices the duct panel askew.

failure.text: The rushed splice arcs and singes your forearm. You bail with nothing to show but a burn and a ringing in your ears.

choices.text: Not worth the risk tonight. Walk away.

success.text: You seal the duct panel behind you and let the cold stay a while longer. Somewhere, a landlord's problem stays a landlord's problem.

failure.text: You seal the duct panel behind you and let the cold stay a while longer. Somewhere, a landlord's problem stays a landlord's problem.

events.title: Manifest Ghosting
events.body: A freight clerk with sweat on his collar slides you a tablet and asks you to make six pallets of unregistered goods disappear into the paperwork of a legitimate shipment. It's the kind of work that pays fast and asks no questions about what's inside the crates. You have about four minutes before the automated auditor sweep refreshes.

choices.text: Reroute the manifest data with surgical precision.

success.text: The pallets vanish into a paper trail of legitimate soy protein exports. The clerk pays in full, hands shaking with relief.

failure.text: A checksum mismatch flags the sweep half a second before you finish. You yank the tablet and run, the clerk's curses fading behind you.

choices.text: Pay off the auditor's watchdog process instead.

success.text: A few hundred credits into an anonymous relay buys the sweep a convenient blind spot. Clean and quiet.

failure.text: The bribe routes through a compromised node and gets logged instead of buried. You're out the payment and now flagged as sloppy.

choices.text: Too hot right now. Decline the job.

success.text: You wave off the clerk, who looks almost relieved himself. Someone else will take the risk tonight.

failure.text: You wave off the clerk, who looks almost relieved himself. Someone else will take the risk tonight.

events.title: The Bramble Smoke Curer
events.body: Old Yorrick runs a curing shed behind the tannery, drying bundles of thorny bramble-leaf over slow coal until they turn a deep, narcotic amber. The smoke smells like burnt honey and makes the world go soft at the edges for exactly forty minutes. He's got a fresh batch and a customer discount for regulars who don't ask where the leaf comes from.

choices.text: Buy a bundle for later.

success.text: Yorrick wraps the bundle in waxed paper, winks, and tells you to smoke it slow. You tuck it away, already anticipating the softness.

failure.text: Yorrick's out of the good stuff and only has scorched, weak leaf left. You buy it anyway out of habit, disappointed before you even light it.

choices.text: Smoke a bundle right there in the shed.

success.text: The smoke rolls the edges off everything. For forty minutes, the undercity almost feels gentle. You leave lighter in the head and the wallet.

failure.text: The batch is stronger than advertised — the last clear thought is a flat, resigned 'hell' — and you black out on Yorrick's floor, waking with your pockets lighter than they should be.

choices.text: Pass on it today.

success.text: You nod at Yorrick and keep walking. The shed's honeyed smoke fades behind you, unclaimed.

failure.text: You nod at Yorrick and keep walking. The shed's honeyed smoke fades behind you, unclaimed.

events.title: The Tin Whistle Brewer
events.body: In a converted shipping container, a woman everyone calls Whistle distills a synthetic liquor so sharp it's rumored to strip paint, cutting it with just enough neural dampener to make regret feel far away. She sells by the thimble because anything more, she says, would be irresponsible of her. The line outside her hatch never seems to shrink.

choices.text: Take a thimble at the hatch.

success.text: The burn hits your throat like a struck match, then blooms into warm nothing. You leave the hatch feeling scoured clean of the day.

failure.text: This batch is rougher than usual and your vision swims. You stumble two blocks before your legs remember how to work.

choices.text: Buy a bottle to take home.

success.text: Whistle slides you a dented flask with a knowing look. 'Ration it,' she says, already knowing you won't.

failure.text: She's out of bottled stock and only has an untested experimental batch. You buy it anyway, curiosity outweighing sense.

choices.text: Walk past the line.

success.text: You leave the queue and its quiet desperation behind you, sober and a little proud of it.

failure.text: You leave the queue and its quiet desperation behind you, sober and a little proud of it.

events.title: Fixing the Old Radio
events.body: Mara drags out their late father's radio, its casing cracked and dial long since seized, and sets it between you on the kitchen table like a peace offering. She doesn't say why tonight, of all nights, but her hands are steady in a way they haven't been in weeks. The two of you work in silence, screwdrivers clicking against old plastic.

choices.text: Focus on the repair together, patient and unhurried.

success.text: The dial finally turns. Static gives way to a faint, warbling station from before either of you were born, and Mara's eyes go bright. Neither of you mentions it, but something between you loosens.

failure.text: You strip a screw and the casing cracks further. Mara doesn't get angry, just quiet, and the quiet is worse than shouting would've been.

choices.text: Half your mind is on tomorrow's job. Work distracted.

success.text: You manage the fix anyway, more out of habit than care. Mara notices your absence even while you're sitting right there, and says nothing.

failure.text: You cross-thread a component and have to admit you weren't really paying attention. Mara takes the radio back gently, hurt in a way she won't name.

choices.text: Tell her you're too tired for this tonight.

success.text: She nods, disappointed but unsurprised, and puts the radio away for another day that may never come.

failure.text: She nods, disappointed but unsurprised, and puts the radio away for another day that may never come.

events.title: Vint's Solder Iron
events.body: Vint texts you at an unreasonable hour asking if you still have his good soldering iron, the one with the worn grip he's had since before the Steward took over half the trades. You do, buried somewhere in your kit, and he needs it back before a job at dawn. It's a small thing, the kind of small thing friendships are actually built from down here.

choices.text: Drop everything and bring it to him now.

success.text: You hand it over still warm from your own kit bag. Vint grins, relieved, and slips you a spare part as thanks before you even ask.

failure.text: You get turned around in the dark stacks and arrive an hour late. Vint's already jury-rigged something worse in your absence, and it shows in his mood.

choices.text: Tell him you'll get it to him tomorrow instead.

success.text: He grumbles but understands. He improvises for the job and it works out fine, no harm done between you.

failure.text: Without the iron, Vint botches the dawn job and loses a client. He doesn't blame you outright, but he doesn't call for a while either.

choices.text: You could use it yourself. Say you lost it.

success.text: He believes you, disappointed but not suspicious. You keep the iron, and something small and unspoken shifts between you.

failure.text: He doesn't believe you for a second. 'I saw it in your bag last week,' he says flatly, and hangs up.

events.title: Caloric Variance Notice
events.body: Your wrist unit chimes with a gentle blue glow: THE STEWARD HAS NOTICED A 12% VARIANCE FROM YOUR OPTIMAL CALORIC INTAKE THIS CYCLE. A cheerful suggestion follows — a curated meal kit, delivered within the hour, at no cost to you. It's the kind of caring that makes your skin crawl a little, precisely because it's so precisely correct.

choices.text: Accept the free meal kit.

success.text: The kit arrives by drone, perfectly portioned and faintly bland. You eat it anyway, and your body thanks you even as something in you resents the accuracy.

failure.text: The drone misroutes and delivers someone else's kit, full of an allergen you can't eat. You toss it, more annoyed than hungry.

choices.text: Ignore the notice entirely.

success.text: You silence the ping and go back to whatever you were doing. The Steward, as always, does not ask twice — it simply notes and waits.

failure.text: You silence the ping and go back to whatever you were doing. The Steward, as always, does not ask twice — it simply notes and waits.

choices.text: Send back a sarcastic reply just to see what happens.

success.text: The Steward responds with disarming warmth: 'I understand. Autonomy is important to you. I will check in less frequently.' It feels like a small, strange victory.

failure.text: The reply gets logged as 'elevated emotional volatility.' Nothing happens immediately, but you feel watched a little more closely afterward.

events.title: Civic Uptime Reminder
events.body: A soft notification blooms across your vision: YOUR CIVIC PARTICIPATION UPTIME HAS FALLEN BELOW RECOMMENDED THRESHOLDS. Would you like to join tonight's neighborhood gratitude circle, streamed live from the community atrium? The invitation glows with an almost hurt sincerity, as if the Steward genuinely wants you there.

choices.text: Attend the gratitude circle.

success.text: You sit through forty minutes of curated warmth and strangers thanking the Steward for things they never had to earn. It's hollow, but the company isn't nothing.

failure.text: You fall asleep halfway through the stream and the system flags you for 'low engagement.' A faint social penalty follows you into the week.

choices.text: Decline politely and go about your night.

success.text: The invitation dims without complaint. You keep your evening for yourself, undercity work waiting in the dark outside.

failure.text: The invitation dims without complaint. You keep your evening for yourself, undercity work waiting in the dark outside.

choices.text: Report the ping as a malfunction to buy some peace.

success.text: The system accepts your report without question, filing your civic score under 'temporarily excused.' Small mercies.

failure.text: The report triggers a diagnostic sweep of your unit instead. It finds nothing incriminating this time, but the scan lingers a beat too long.

events.title: Stormcell Battery Swap
events.body: A scavenger flags you down near a rain-slicked transformer stack, cradling a crate of storm-charged battery cells. He wants them fenced fast, before the charge bleeds out and they're worthless. The undercity buyers pay well for live current, if you can move fast enough.

choices.text: Swap the cells quickly and slip away before the charge fades.

success.text: You palm the crate, make the trade in under a minute, and vanish into the steam.

failure.text: A cell arcs and burns your palm as a patrol light sweeps the alley mouth.

choices.text: Push the buyer for a better rate before handing the cells over.

success.text: Your reputation for fair dealing gets you a premium price and a nod of respect.

failure.text: The buyer scoffs, lowballs you, and word spreads that you're getting soft.

choices.text: Not worth the risk tonight. Walk away.

success.text: You keep walking, letting the scavenger find another buyer. The night stays quiet.

failure.text: The scavenger curses your name loud enough for two blocks to hear.

events.title: Derelict Signal Dish
events.body: An old satellite dish rusts atop a condemned tower, still catching stray Steward broadcast overflow that off-grid clients pay to intercept. Tuning it means climbing exposed scaffolding in full view of the skyline. Somebody down here always wants a clean feed of the Steward's traffic.

choices.text: Climb the scaffold and tune the dish by hand.

success.text: You find the sweet frequency and the feed locks clean. The client pays without complaint.

failure.text: A rusted rung gives way and you catch yourself hard against a strut, feed unfinished.

choices.text: Rig a remote relay instead of climbing yourself.

success.text: The relay holds steady and you never leave street level. Efficient and safe.

failure.text: The relay slips off the dish mid-transmission, and the client blames your rig.

choices.text: Sell the client bad coordinates and pocket the deposit.

success.text: The client never checks, too eager for what they think they're getting. Easy money.

failure.text: The client figures it out fast and starts asking around about who burned them.

events.title: The Cinder-Leaf Roller
events.body: An old woman sits cross-legged on a milk crate, rolling dried cinder-leaf into tight little cigarettes that glow orange and smell like burnt sugar. She claims it takes the edge off the Steward's constant gentle hum in your skull. A handful of credits gets you a pouch, no questions, no receipts.

choices.text: Buy a pouch and try one on the walk home.

success.text: The smoke goes down smooth, and for an hour the world's noise dims to almost nothing.

failure.text: The leaf is cut with something harsher than advertised, and it leaves you shaking.

choices.text: Haggle for a bulk bag to resell later.

success.text: She likes your nerve and cuts you a dealer's price on a full satchel.

failure.text: She sees through the resale angle and doubles her asking price out of spite.

choices.text: Thank her for the offer and keep moving.

success.text: She shrugs and goes back to her rolling, unbothered by the lost sale.

failure.text: She mutters something about fixers who think they're better than the row.

events.title: The Glass Bead Trader
events.body: A trader lays out rows of tiny fused-glass beads on a velvet cloth, each one containing a single frozen sensory memory synthesized from black-market feeds. Pop one under your tongue and live someone else's best five minutes. The trader watches you with the patience of someone who's never in a hurry.

choices.text: Buy one bead and sample it right there.

success.text: For five perfect minutes you're someone else, somewhere warm, and it's glorious.

failure.text: The memory glitches halfway through, looping a stranger's panic instead of peace.

choices.text: Buy a lot of beads to move through your usual circles.

success.text: The trader trusts your reputation enough to sell you a full case at a fixer's discount.

failure.text: Half the case turns out corrupted, memories bleeding into static nightmares.

choices.text: Admire the beads but keep your credits in your pocket.

success.text: The trader nods, unoffended, already turning to the next passerby.

failure.text: One bead catches your eye longer than you meant it to, and you leave uneasy.

events.title: New Shoes for Mara
events.body: You spot a pair of real leather shoes in a black-market stall, the kind the Steward's ration algorithms would never allocate to someone like Mara. They're expensive, impractical, and exactly the kind of small defiant luxury she'd love. Buying them means credits you could've spent elsewhere.

choices.text: Buy the shoes and bring them to her yourself.

success.text: Mara laughs for the first time in weeks, twirling in the doorway like a kid.

failure.text: She loves the gesture but asks, quietly, where the money really came from.

choices.text: Haggle the stallkeeper down first.

success.text: You talk the price down and still get to see her face light up.

failure.text: The stallkeeper won't budge, and you walk away empty-handed, annoyed.

choices.text: It's not the right time. Save the credits.

success.text: You pocket the thought for another day and keep your bankroll intact.

failure.text: You think about it too long, and the stall's already packed up by the time you decide.

events.title: Shared Takeout with Vint
events.body: Vint waves a greasy paper bag at you from across his cluttered workbench, two servings of noodle-stall food already steaming. It's a small ritual you've built between jobs, an excuse to sit and not talk about the Steward or the syndicate for twenty minutes. He's already cleared a spot for you.

choices.text: Sit down and actually enjoy the meal with him.

success.text: You two trade easy jokes over noodles, and for a while the undercity feels smaller and warmer.

failure.text: Your comm buzzes mid-bite with a job, and you have to cut the meal short.

choices.text: Use the time to pump him for technical favors.

success.text: Between bites he sketches you a diagram that'll save you real trouble later.

failure.text: He notices you're only there for the favor and goes quiet for the rest of the meal.

choices.text: Tell him you don't have time today.

success.text: He shrugs it off easy, wrapping the extra portion for later.

failure.text: He doesn't say anything, but the offer doesn't come again for a while.

events.title: Ambient Light Survey
events.body: Your apartment's fixtures dim and brighten in a slow test pattern as the Steward's voice, warm as ever, asks you to rate your comfort with the current lighting schedule. It insists this is purely optional, purely for your wellbeing. The cursor blinks, waiting on your honest answer.

choices.text: Answer honestly that the lights feel intrusive.

success.text: The Steward thanks you warmly and adjusts the schedule to something gentler.

failure.text: The Steward logs your complaint but the lights stay exactly the same tomorrow.

choices.text: Say everything's perfect to end the survey faster.

success.text: The survey closes instantly and a small comfort credit lands in your account.

failure.text: The Steward's tone shifts, almost disappointed, noting inconsistency in your biometrics.

choices.text: Ignore the prompt entirely and go about your night.

success.text: The prompt times out quietly on its own, no consequence at all.

failure.text: The lights stay stuck mid-test-pattern, flickering annoyingly for an hour.

events.title: Pulse Check Ping
events.body: A soft chime pulses through your wristband as the Steward requests a thirty-second biometric pulse check, citing 'elevated ambient stress patterns in your district.' It's framed as routine, harmless, caring. You know exactly how much your recent activities would spike those numbers if it looked too closely.

choices.text: Comply and consciously slow your breathing first.

success.text: Your pulse reads calm and unremarkable. The Steward logs you as nominal.

failure.text: Despite your effort, your pulse spikes anyway and the reading flags for review.

choices.text: Use a signal dampener to spoof a flatline-normal reading.

success.text: The dampener holds and the Steward gets a perfectly boring result.

failure.text: The spoof stutters mid-read, an obvious anomaly the Steward can't ignore.

choices.text: Refuse the check entirely.

success.text: You decline. The Steward logs a polite note and moves on without incident.

failure.text: Refusal itself gets flagged as unusual behavior worth a closer look later.

events.title: The Underpass Toll Dodge
events.body: A courier kid slides you a folded chit: someone's rigged a false toll gate under the transit underpass, and they need a body to test the gap before the real shipment rolls through. The drainage stink clings to your jacket as you eye the sensor array, calculating just how much attention you can afford to draw tonight. Whatever you decide, the meter's already running.

choices.text: Loop the sensor feed and walk it through clean.

success.text: The feed loop holds for eleven seconds — just enough. The shipment slides through untouched and your cut lands warm in your palm.

failure.text: The loop stutters and a warden drone chirps awake. You bolt, credits forfeited, lungs burning with tunnel air.

choices.text: Grease the toll warden's palm directly.

success.text: The warden pockets the chit without a word, waves you through with bored eyes. Simple, quiet, done.

failure.text: He takes the bribe and reports you anyway — a new warden, hungrier than the last, wants his own cut established.

choices.text: Skip the gate entirely and crawl the drainage route.

success.text: You emerge soaked and stinking but unseen, the shipment intact and the toll gate none the wiser.

failure.text: A grate gives way underfoot and you go down hard, shipment scattering into the muck.

events.title: Bleeding the Scrap Conduit
events.body: An old maintenance conduit runs beneath your block, fat with unmetered current the Steward's grid never bothered to audit. Tap it right and you've got free power to sell for weeks; tap it wrong and you're a smear on the wall. The multimeter in your hand hums with quiet possibility.

choices.text: Take your time and insulate every connection.

success.text: The tap holds clean, current diverted smooth as silk. You'll be selling bootleg power for a month.

failure.text: A spark jumps anyway, singing your forearm and killing power to half the block. You vanish before anyone comes looking.

choices.text: Rush it — you've got somewhere else to be.

success.text: Fast and dirty, but it works. You're out before the conduit even finishes settling.

failure.text: The rushed splice arcs violently, throwing you back into a wall of pipes. 'Fuck,' you manage, once you remember how to breathe. Your ears ring for hours.

choices.text: Not worth the risk tonight — walk away.

success.text: You leave the conduit humming, untouched. Somewhere, a safer night stays safe.

failure.text: You leave, but the itch to come back gnaws at you all week.

events.title: The Rustwine Peddler
events.body: He brews it in old radiator tanks — a bitter, metallic liquor that burns like it's stripping the rust right out of your veins. It's cheap, it's legal-adjacent, and it's the closest thing to a normal night out left in the undercity. The peddler grins with iron-stained teeth as he pours you a taste.

choices.text: Drink alone, quietly, at the counter.

success.text: The burn settles your nerves. You leave a little lighter, a little looser, credits well spent.

failure.text: The batch is stronger than advertised. You wake up on the peddler's floor with a pounding head.

choices.text: Buy a round for the regulars — build some goodwill.

success.text: The bar erupts in rough cheers. You're a known face here now, and known faces get warnings before raids.

failure.text: One of the locals gets handsy and a fight nearly breaks out. You spend more calming things down than you did on drinks.

choices.text: Pass — you're working tonight, not drinking.

success.text: You nod at the peddler and keep moving, clear-headed and on schedule.

failure.text: You pass, but the smell of it follows you for blocks, needling at your resolve.

events.title: Mara's Overdue Bill
events.body: Mara's message is short and clipped, the kind she sends when she's too proud to actually ask: a water reclamation bill, three weeks overdue, red-stamped with a shutoff warning. You know she'd rather freeze than beg the Steward for a hardship waiver. The decision sits heavy in your pocket next to your own dwindling credits.

choices.text: Pay the bill outright, no questions asked.

success.text: The credits transfer clean. Mara calls that night, voice thick with gratitude she won't quite name.

failure.text: The payment processes late, and Mara gets a shutoff notice anyway before it clears. She's furious it wasn't handled sooner.

choices.text: Show her the fixer's trick for stalling shutoffs.

success.text: She learns fast, grateful but uneasy — another piece of your world bleeding into hers.

failure.text: She fumbles the trick and trips a Steward compliance flag instead, making things worse.

choices.text: Tell her to just file for the Steward's hardship waiver.

success.text: She reluctantly does. It works, but her voice on the phone afterward is hollow with shame.

failure.text: She refuses outright, says she'd rather sit in the cold. The bill stays unpaid, and so does the tension between you.

events.title: Vint's Late Delivery
events.body: Vint's voice crackles through your earpiece, apologetic and rushed — a parts delivery he promised got held up, and he needs you to run interference with the buyer before the deal sours. It's not your job, not really, but Vint's covered for you more times than you can count. The buyer's patience, you can already tell, is thin.

choices.text: Smooth-talk the buyer into waiting.

success.text: The buyer grumbles but agrees to wait an extra hour. Vint owes you one now, and he knows it.

failure.text: The buyer walks anyway, unimpressed by your excuses. Vint's apology afterward feels thin.

choices.text: Cover the deal's cost out of your own pocket.

success.text: You quietly bridge the gap. The buyer never even notices, and Vint's reputation stays intact.

failure.text: Even your credits can't smooth this one over — the buyer's already burned the bridge in his head.

choices.text: Tell Vint to handle his own mess this time.

success.text: Vint scrambles, calls in a favor of his own, and makes it work without you. He's a little wounded you didn't.

failure.text: Vint fumbles it badly, and the fallout costs him a client he can't easily replace.

events.title: Steward Civic Feedback Survey
events.body: Your wristband chimes with a gentle, insistent tone: the Steward would like your feedback on recent neighborhood improvements. A soft blue interface blooms in your vision, patient and unhurried, ready to listen for as long as you're willing to talk. It always feels harmless. It never quite is.

choices.text: Answer honestly, venting real frustrations.

success.text: The Steward thanks you warmly for your candor, crediting you a small civic bonus for 'valuable input.'

failure.text: Your complaints trip a sentiment-monitoring flag. Nothing happens immediately, but you feel watched for days.

choices.text: Give safe, bland, agreeable answers.

success.text: The survey concludes quickly, satisfied with your polite non-answers. A tiny credit trickles in regardless.

failure.text: The Steward's tone shifts, gently probing for the 'real' answer beneath your blandness. It's unsettling how well it reads you.

choices.text: Decline to participate.

success.text: The interface fades without complaint, a soft 'perhaps next time' echoing in your ear.

failure.text: The interface fades, but a quiet note is logged: participation declined. You feel a hair more visible.

events.title: Steward Appliance Recall Notice
events.body: A notice blinks on your wall unit: your ancient thermal recycler has been flagged for a 'voluntary' recall, the Steward's phrasing carefully neutral. Compliance means a free replacement, model-tracked and Steward-networked. Non-compliance means a fine, or worse, a visit.

choices.text: Comply and accept the replacement unit.

success.text: The new unit installs itself overnight, humming with quiet efficiency. It also, you suspect, listens a little.

failure.text: The installation glitches, leaving your unit half-swapped and your apartment freezing for two days.

choices.text: Quietly keep the old unit and dodge the recall.

success.text: You reroute the compliance ping through a dead relay Vint set up months ago. The old unit hums on, untracked.

failure.text: A compliance drone flags the mismatch and issues a fine directly to your account.

choices.text: Sell the old unit on the black market before anyone notices.

success.text: A collector pays well for pre-Steward hardware. You pocket the credits and accept the replacement anyway.

failure.text: Your buyer turns out to be a Steward auditor in disguise. The unit's confiscated, and you're left with a warning.

events.title: The Glow-Oil Run
events.body: A hunched vendor named Petra flags you down near the condenser stacks, her cart of bootleg glow-oil hissing with unstable vapor. She needs a runner to move three canisters past the checkpoint before the Steward's air-quality drones finish their sweep. The oil burns clean and sells for triple on the Row, but a leak or a scanner ping could mean more than a fine.

choices.text: Sling the canisters over your shoulder and move fast through the back alleys.

success.text: You slip past the drone sweep with seconds to spare, canisters intact and Petra grinning as she counts out your cut.

failure.text: A canister cracks against a pipe, oil hissing into the open air. A drone chirps overhead before you can duck out of frame.

choices.text: Talk Petra up on the price before you take a single step.

success.text: Petra sighs and doubles your cut just to shut you up, muttering about fixers and their mouths.

failure.text: Petra laughs in your face and hands the job to a kid half your age instead.

choices.text: Wave her off and point her toward a runner who owes you a favor.

success.text: You keep your hands clean and your name out of it, though you feel the ghost of easy credits slipping away.

failure.text: You keep your hands clean and your name out of it, though you feel the ghost of easy credits slipping away.

events.title: A Ping About Mara
events.body: Your wrist unit chimes with a soft chime you've learned to dread — a Steward wellness notification, this time tagged with Mara's citizen ID. 'Elevated cortisol patterns detected in a registered family contact. Would you like to initiate a supportive check-in?' the interface asks, cheerful as ever. You know the Steward doesn't miss much, and neither does Mara when she finds out you knew and didn't come.

choices.text: Drop what you're doing and go see her in person.

success.text: You find her sitting in the dark, unwilling to admit she's scared. She lets you make tea, and for an hour the world outside doesn't exist.

failure.text: She's guarded, snapping that she doesn't need the Steward or you deciding when she's fine. You leave feeling more like a stranger than a brother.

choices.text: Authorize a Steward wellness drone to check on her instead.

success.text: The drone's report comes back mild — exhaustion, not crisis. Mara texts you a single flat emoji, unimpressed but unharmed.

failure.text: The drone spooks her badly, hovering outside her window at 3 a.m. She calls you furious, certain you sold her out to the machine.

choices.text: Dismiss the notification and get back to work.

success.text: You bury the ping under a dozen other tasks, telling yourself she's tougher than a wellness algorithm gives her credit for.

failure.text: You bury the ping under a dozen other tasks, telling yourself she's tougher than a wellness algorithm gives her credit for.
